dims.title: Pre-registered matched-exposure test of the chop rule and the vol target
dims.task:
PRE-REGISTERED TEST. Question: do the chop rule (half size when er20 < 0.25) and the volatility target add value beyond simply holding less exposure? Round-1 critic found the chop rule drives 61-66% of turnover and its tranche Calmar benefit is only +0.03 (F2) / +0.07 (F3).
Setup: tiers F2 (qld, vt .30) and F3 (tqqq, vt .20), IEF off-leg, gold_phys 15%, cost 3 bps, lag 1. PRIMARY basis = 5-weekday tranche; also report the Friday book.
(a) CHOP RULE. Baseline B = rules as specified. Alternative A = NO chop rule (engine = scale whenever risk-on) with the vol target lowered so that A's average NDX exposure equals B's over 1988-01-01..2026-07-24 (exposure = leverage x sleeve weight, averaged over all days; solve by bisection on voltgt, separately for each tier and basis). Also report A0 = no chop at the original vol target (reference only).
(b) VOL TARGET. Baseline B vs alternative V = NO vol scaling (engine = 1 when risk-on, still with chop half-size and Aug-Sep half) times a constant c chosen so V's average NDX exposure equals B's.
CROSS-MARKET (same constructions, 2x tier only, vt .30 baseline): S&P 500 (spx), Russell 2000 (rut), TSX (tsx), Hang Seng (hsi) from the panel (rebuild price = cumprod(1+r) for signals), plus DAX (^GDAXI), Nikkei 225 (^N225) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fetched from yfinance; each market uses its own price for EMA-100/vol20/er20; sleeve = 2*r - 0.95%/252 - rf_d; same IEF + 15% gold_phys off-legs; tranche basis; period 1990-01-01 (or first full year available) to 2026-07-24.
PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE (apply exactly): A component is RETAINED if, on the tranche basis, B beats its matched-exposure alternative by Calmar >= +0.03 in BOTH halves (1988-01-01..2006-12-31 and 2007-01-01..2026-07-24) for the tier in question AND the cross-market median Calmar difference (B minus matched alternative) is >= +0.02. It is REPLACEABLE (acts only as a de-levering dial) if B's Calmar edge is < +0.03 in at least one half AND the cross-market median difference is <= +0.02. Any other combination = INCONCLUSIVE (retain by default). Apply the rule separately to chop and vol target, for F2 and for F3.
Also report for B vs A: annual one-way turnover, number of trades, results at 10 and 15 bps per unit turnover (the UCITS route), Ulcer index, mean of the 5 worst drawdowns, CDaR95, and OOS (2026-07-25..end) as information only. State the decisions plainly in the headline.

result.headline: Pre-registered decisions (5-weekday tranche, 3 bps, data to 2026-07-24): the CHOP RULE is REPLACEABLE for F2 and F3. The VOL TARGET is REPLACEABLE for F2 and INCONCLUSIVE (retained by default) for F3. Against the same average exposure, both components add Calmar only in NDX 1988-2006: the chop rule mainly in 1988-99, the vol target only in the 2000 crash. In 2007-2026 the difference is between -0.012 and +0.034. Across 7 other indices the median Calmar difference is +0.011 for chop and -0.001 for the vol target. Both components are de-levering dials, not sources of edge.
decisions: Primary basis is the 5-weekday tranche, built exactly as main_tranche_check.py (the average of the five weekday books' daily net returns). It reproduces main_tranche_check.json exactly: F2 17.29% / -27.7% / Calmar 0.625; F3 20.88% / -32.5% / 0.643 (1988-01-01 to 2026-07-24). The Friday book is reported as secondary, information only.

Exposure = leverage x the leveraged-sleeve weight actually held (one-day lag), averaged over every trading day including risk-off days, 1988-01-01 to 2026-07-24. For the tranche it is the average of the 5 books.

A (no chop rule): the vol target was solved by bisection to 1e-12 (exposure error at most 2e-12), separately for each tier and basis. V (no vol scaling) times a constant c: c was solved directly because exposure is exactly linear in c, then re-checked. Neither solver used any return data (1002 exposure-only evaluations).
The halves are evaluated with the A and V matched over the full period, as pre-registered. Re-matching exposure inside each half is reported as information only.

The cross-market median uses the 7 listed indices: spx, rut, tsx, hsi, ^GDAXI, ^N225, ^IXIC. Simulated 2x NDX is shown as a reference row and excluded from the median. Every market starts on 1990-01-01 (a one-year warm-up rule never bound), and exposure is matched over 1990-01-01 to 2026-07-24.

The yfinance indices are local-currency closes, forward-filled onto the panel's US trading calendar, with no FX conversion. Yahoo returned HTTP 429 at first; the fetch succeeded on retry and is cached in update_2026_11/r2_chop_vol_matched_yf.parquet.

Turnover follows the common.py convention: the sum over sleeves of the change in held weight per year (called one-way turnover). A trade is any sleeve weight change above 1e-6. Tranche trade counts are summed over the 5 books and also reported per book.

CDaR95 = the average of the worst 5% of daily drawdown values. 'Mean of the 5 worst drawdowns' = the 5 deepest separate drawdowns, each ending at a new equity high. Ulcer = the root-mean-square of percent drawdowns.

The decision rule was applied exactly as written, at 3 bps. The following are information only and changed no decision: results at 10/15 bps, the Friday book, the constant-multiplier alternative Ac, the 3x / vt .20 cross-market run, the bootstrap, within-half re-matching and the single-weekday books.

Variant count: 157 in total. That is 127 variants whose returns were evaluated (NDX 24; within-half re-match 20; cross-market 48, including the NDX-sim reference and Ac; 3x information run 35) plus 30 single-weekday information runs.

claims.claim: Pre-registered outcomes (tranche basis, in-sample): the chop rule is REPLACEABLE for F2 and F3; the vol target is REPLACEABLE for F2 and INCONCLUSIVE (retained by default) for F3. The outcomes are the same at 10 and 15 bps.
claims.evidence: Chop, Calmar difference B minus A: F2 H1 +0.2444 / H2 -0.0119; F3 +0.1554 / +0.0069. H2 is below +0.03 for both, and the cross-market median is +0.0106 (at most +0.02), so REPLACEABLE. Vol, B minus V: F2 +0.2485 / -0.0023, median -0.0005, so REPLACEABLE. F3 +0.1587 / +0.0341: both halves are at least +0.03, but the median of -0.0005 is below +0.02, so INCONCLUSIVE.

claims.claim: At matched exposure, the chop rule's edge comes from one era and one market. In-sample it is strongly positive only on NDX in 1988-99. It is negative in most other markets in 1990-2006 and close to zero everywhere in 2007-2026.
claims.evidence: NDX tranche B minus A, F2: 1988-99 +0.436, 2000-12 -0.111, 2013-freeze -0.012 (F3: +0.280 / +0.040 / +0.006). Cross-market 2x, 1990-2006: median -0.117, negative in 6 of 7 markets. 2007-2026: median +0.010, positive in 7 of 7 but at most +0.055. Full period by market: spx -0.002, rut -0.006, tsx +0.079, hsi +0.011, dax +0.020, n225 +0.041, ixic -0.066.

claims.claim: The vol target's in-sample value is essentially one episode: the March 2000 Nasdaq top, when volatility spiked while NDX was still above its EMA-100. In 2007-2026 it changes almost nothing.
claims.evidence: F2 tranche worst drawdown in H1: B -23.4% (1989-10-09 to 1990-05-02) vs V -34.0% (2000-03-09 to 2000-10-04). In H2 both have the same -27.7% (2021-11-19 to 2022-10-20). The target is active on 16.2% (H1) and 4.2% (H2) of F2 risk-on days; for F3, 42.9% and 22.8%. Cross-market vol differences are within +/-0.007 everywhere except ixic (+0.102) and the NDX-sim reference (+0.117).

claims.claim: Measuring the components on the Friday book inflates their value through rebalance-timing luck. Friday is the most favourable weekday for both components in both tiers.
claims.evidence: In-sample Calmar difference by single-weekday book, chop F2 Mon..Fri: +0.015 / +0.039 / +0.076 / +0.115 / +0.218; F3: +0.050 / +0.060 / +0.087 / +0.057 / +0.237; vol F2: +0.171 / +0.002 / +0.095 / +0.042 / +0.244. On the Friday book chop passes both halves (H2 +0.083 for F2, +0.099 for F3); on the tranche it fails (-0.012 and +0.007).

claims.claim: Information only: a plain constant de-levering multiplier (Ac = no chop rule, original vol target, all positions scaled to match exposure) does as well as the chop rule on the tranche, with about half the turnover.
claims.evidence: Ac multiplier 0.715 (F2) / 0.719 (F3). In-sample tranche Calmar 0.620 vs B 0.625 (F2) and 0.616 vs 0.643 (F3). Calmar difference H1 / H2: F2 +0.050 / +0.005, F3 +0.023 / +0.016. Cross-market median +0.005, so the same REPLACEABLE verdict. Turnover 6.81 vs 12.87 a year (F2); rebalances 10.3 vs 18.3 per book per year.

claims.claim: The chop rule is expensive in turnover. At UCITS-route costs, its 2007-2026 deficit against the matched alternative widens.
claims.evidence: Tranche one-way turnover a year, B / A: F2 12.87 / 8.99; F3 12.48 / 8.70. A trades about twice as often in smaller amounts: 35.0 vs 18.3 rebalances per book per year (F2), average leveraged-sleeve trade 12.8% vs 35.1% of NAV. Chop H2 Calmar difference: F2 -0.012 at 3 bps, -0.023 at 10 bps, -0.031 at 15 bps; F3 +0.007 / -0.003 / -0.010. Cross-market chop median: +0.011 / +0.002 / -0.003.

claims.claim: Drawdown-shape metrics show no chop advantage at matched exposure. The vol target does improve them in-sample, mainly because of 2000.
claims.evidence: In-sample tranche, B vs A: Ulcer 9.57 vs 9.16 (F2) and 13.59 vs 13.46 (F3); mean of 5 worst drawdowns -22.6% vs -21.8% and -28.9% vs -29.1%; CDaR95 -20.9% vs -20.3% and -26.5% vs -27.4%. B vs V: Ulcer 9.57 vs 11.28 and 13.59 vs 18.31; CDaR95 -20.9% vs -28.4% and -26.5% vs -41.5%; max drawdown -27.7% vs -34.0% and -32.5% vs -47.4%.

claims.claim: None of the in-sample Calmar differences can be told apart from noise.
claims.evidence: Paired 63-day block bootstrap, 1000 draws, in-sample tranche Calmar difference. Chop F2: mean +0.086 (5th-95th percentile -0.047 to +0.233), probability of zero or worse 0.13. Chop F3: +0.071, probability 0.11. Vol F2: +0.039, probability 0.32. Vol F3: +0.025, probability 0.42. IXIC and simulated 2x NDX give opposite chop signs (-0.066 vs +0.054).

claims.claim: The F3 vol-target INCONCLUSIVE verdict sits on a knife edge. The registered cross-market leg has little power for the vol target. A more powerful information-only version still would not give RETAINED.
claims.evidence: F3 H2 difference is +0.0341 against the +0.03 bar; re-matching exposure inside H2 gives +0.029, which would fail. At the registered 2x / vt .30 the target is active on only 0.9-9.3% of risk-on days in the 7 markets (matching multiplier 0.983-0.999). The information-only 3x / vt .20 run (target active 5.5-30.6%) gives a vol median of +0.012 (4 of 7 positive), still below +0.02, and a chop median of -0.001.

claims.claim: Out-of-sample (2026-07-25 to 2026-11-17, information only): the matched no-chop alternative A lost less than B on every basis, and V tracked B.
claims.evidence: Total return B / A / V: F2 tranche -10.69% / -8.55% / -10.54%; F3 tranche -14.91% / -11.09% / -13.83%; F2 Friday -6.03% / -1.77% / -5.95%; F3 Friday -8.99% / -2.13% / -7.65%. This window is 81 trading days.

claims.claim: The mechanics were checked independently and agree with the shared code and round-1 outputs.
claims.evidence: Numpy engine vs common.backtest: largest daily difference 0 (Friday) and 2.8e-17 (tranche). main_tranche_check.json is reproduced exactly. The critic's unmatched ablations are reproduced to 4.6e-6 (no chop at the original vol target vs B: F2 +0.029, F3 +0.072). Cross-market rows recomputed through common.py agree to 2.8e-17. NDX signals rebuilt from returns differ from the panel on 0 days.

result.recommendation:
Read these verdicts as a classification, not as an instruction to change the frozen rules. Keep the July rules unchanged for the IBKR paper build: no exposure-matched alternative beats B in-sample on the tranche. The matched alternative A (no chop rule, vol target lowered) has a Calmar 0.055 lower for F2 and 0.119 lower for F3; the constant multiplier Ac ties within 0.03. But stop counting the chop rule or the vol target as sources of edge. They are exposure dials; the edge that survives is the EMA-100 gate on leveraged Nasdaq. Set expectations on the tranche basis (F2 17.3% CAGR, -27.7% max drawdown, Calmar 0.62; F3 20.9%, -32.5%, 0.64), not on the Friday book.

Keep the vol target in both tiers, even though the rule calls it REPLACEABLE for F2. Removing it saves almost no turnover (12.87 vs 12.77 a year). It is also the only component that cut the 2000-type crash: F3 max drawdown is -32.5% with it and -47.4% without.

The one simplification with a practical payoff is replacing the chop rule with a constant exposure multiplier of about 0.71x. That roughly halves turnover (F2 6.8 vs 12.9 a year), which matters on the UCITS route: at 15 bps, F2 tranche Calmar is 0.576 with the multiplier vs 0.549 with the chop rule. Because 0.71 would be a new parameter, it needs its own pre-registered test before adoption.
caveats: Calmar is set by the single worst drawdown, so each half's verdict rests on one or two episodes. Chop's H1 edge comes from the 1989-90 drawdown plus higher 1990s CAGR (F2 H1 CAGR: B 18.03% vs A 13.78%). The vol target's H1 edge comes from 2000-03 to 2000-10.

Possible rule flaw (vol target): at the registered 2x / vt .30 setup, the vol target is active on only 0.9-9.3% of risk-on days in the 7 markets. The cross-market leg therefore has almost no power and passes 'at most +0.02' nearly by construction. The information-only 3x / vt .20 run (target active 5.5-30.6% of risk-on days) gives a median of +0.012, so no verdict would change.

Possible rule flaw (chop): the registered alternative A lowers the vol target to about 0.11-0.12. At that level the target is active on most risk-on days, so A is a volatility-timed strategy rather than simply 'less exposure'. The information-only constant multiplier Ac gives the same REPLACEABLE verdict.
The F3 vol-target INCONCLUSIVE verdict is on a knife edge: H2 is +0.0341 against the +0.03 bar. Re-matching exposure inside H2 gives +0.029, which would flip it to REPLACEABLE.

The 0.03-per-half threshold is small next to sampling noise: the bootstrap's 5th-95th percentile ranges are about 0.18-0.28 wide. Near-identical indices disagree in sign (IXIC chop -0.066 vs simulated NDX +0.054).
A makes about twice as many, smaller trades as B (35 vs 18 rebalances per book per year for F2). With fixed per-order fees, A's cost advantage shrinks; costs proportional to turnover favour A and Ac.

Foreign markets use local-currency indices (DAX is a total-return index), US T-bill financing and the US-listed IEF and gold off-legs, all on the US trading calendar. HSI has 11-14 forward-filled zero-return days a year. These affect return levels, not the B-vs-alternative comparison within each market.
Gold before 2000-08-30 is the monthly interpolation. It enters only as the same 15% return sleeve in every variant, never as a signal.
The out-of-sample window (2026-07-25 to 2026-11-17) is 81 trading days and is information only.

verifications.lens: INTEGRITY. I re-ran the script and it reproduces the saved JSON exactly: 0 differing leaves, with output redirected to scratch so the original JSON was not touched. I then wrote an independent re-implementation: weights built from the spec text, held weights and backtest from common.py, tranche = mean of the 5 weekday books, vt_A solved by Illinois regula-falsi instead of bisection, and all 7 cross-market indices plus the NDX-sim reference rebuilt with my own data path. I ran it on the full panel and again on the panel truncated at 2026-07-24. Both runs match all 96 compared quantities to 5.6e-13: vt_A, c_V, the Calmar differences at 3/10/15 bps for both tiers and both bases, the 7 market rows and both medians. Check scripts: update_2026_11/r2_verify_chop_vol_matched_integrity_{rerun,checks,sens,episode}.py.
verifications.rule_applied_correctly: Yes, the rule was applied exactly as written. decide() returns RETAINED only if both halves are >= +0.03 AND the median is >= +0.02, REPLACEABLE if at least one half is < +0.03 AND the median is <= +0.02, and INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. It runs on the tranche basis at 3 bps, with H1 = 1988-01-01..2006-12-31 and H2 = 2007-01-01..2026-07-24, exposure matched over the full in-sample period, and the 2x / vt .30 7-index median over 1990-01-01..2026-07-24 (NDX-sim excluded). My independent rebuild gives the same four verdicts, and so does the run truncated at the freeze. Chop F2: H1 +0.2444, H2 -0.0119, median +0.01056, REPLACEABLE. Chop F3: +0.1554 / +0.0069, REPLACEABLE. Vol F2: +0.2485 / -0.0023, median -0.00053, REPLACEABLE. Vol F3: +0.1587 / +0.0341, INCONCLUSIVE. The F3 vol margin is only +0.0041 at 3 bps (+0.0012 at 10 bps, +0.00004 at 15 bps). It does not change if exposure is measured on target instead of held weights (+0.0341), with pre-2000 gold set to zero or to month-end lumps, or with Yahoo ^HSI in place of the panel's hsi (median +0.0109).

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly by the re-run and by the independent common.py rebuild, on both the full and the truncated panel (max difference 5.6e-13). H1/H2 differences: chop F2 +0.2444/-0.0119, chop F3 +0.1554/+0.0069, vol F2 +0.2485/-0.0023, vol F3 +0.1587/+0.0341. Medians: chop +0.0106, vol -0.0005. Verdicts: REPLACEABLE, REPLACEABLE, REPLACEABLE, INCONCLUSIVE. Unchanged at 10/15 bps, though F3 vol H2 is then +0.0312 and +0.03004, the latter 0.00004 above the bar.

Every number reproduces. NDX F2 by era: +0.436 / -0.111 / -0.012; F3: +0.280 / +0.040 / +0.006. Cross-market 1990-2006: median -0.117, 6 of 7 negative. 2007-26: median +0.0096, 7 of 7 positive, maximum +0.055 (TSX). The wording 'one era and one market ... strongly positive only on NDX in 1988-99' is contradicted by N225 in 1990-2006: chop difference +0.198 (B Calmar 0.403 vs A 0.204; max drawdown -20.9% vs -25.5%), which is larger than NDX F3's H1 +0.155. TSX is also +0.079 over the full period and +0.055 in 2007-26.
verdicts.corrected: The chop rule's edge at matched exposure is concentrated on NDX 1988-99 (F2 +0.436, F3 +0.280) and on N225 1990-2006 (+0.198). It is negative in the other 6 markets in 1990-2006 (7-market median -0.117) and small in 2007-26 (median +0.010, largest TSX +0.055).

verdicts.reason: The cited numbers reproduce. F2 V's H1 max drawdown is -34.0% (2000-03-09 to 2000-10-04) vs B's -23.4% (1989-90); in H2 both are -27.7%. Vol-target binding: 16.2% / 4.2% of risk-on days (F2) and 42.9% / 22.8% (F3). Cross-market vol differences are within +/-0.0072 except ixic +0.102 and the NDX-sim reference +0.117. NDX was above its EMA-100 with vol20 0.38-0.57 from 2000-03-03 to 2000-04-07, and March-April 2000 gives about 62% of the 2000 V-minus-B return gap. In 1988-99 the vol target is negative at matched exposure (-0.050 F2, -0.242 F3). But the edge is not one episode. In the 2001-02 sub-period B minus V is +0.148 (F2) and +0.418 (F3); December 2002 alone has a V-minus-B gap of -3.6pp / -8.7pp; F3 V's H1 trough is 2003-04-09. 'Changes almost nothing in 2007-26' holds for F2 (-0.002) but not F3 (+0.034), which clears the +0.03 bar and is what makes F3 INCONCLUSIVE.
verdicts.corrected: The vol target's in-sample value comes from the 2000-02 dot-com bust: 2000 sets the H1 max drawdown, and 2001-02 adds +0.148 (F2) / +0.418 (F3). It is negative in 1988-99 (-0.050 / -0.242). In 2007-26 the difference is -0.002 for F2 and +0.034 for F3.

verdicts.reason: Single-weekday differences reproduce: chop F2 +0.015/+0.039/+0.076/+0.115/+0.218; chop F3 +0.050/+0.060/+0.087/+0.057/+0.237; vol F2 +0.171/+0.002/+0.095/+0.042/+0.244. Vol F3, not stated in the claim, is +0.194/+0.098/+0.174/+0.023/+0.256. Re-matching exposure separately for each book changes the values by at most 0.002, and Friday remains the largest in all four component-tier cases. Friday-book chop H2: +0.083 (F2), +0.099 (F3); tranche: -0.012 / +0.007.

The numbers reproduce exactly. c_Ac = 0.7148 / 0.7190. In-sample Calmar Ac 0.620 vs B 0.625 (F2) and 0.616 vs 0.643 (F3). Differences H1/H2: +0.050/+0.005 (F2), +0.023/+0.016 (F3). Cross-market median +0.0052, so also REPLACEABLE. Turnover 6.81 vs 12.87 a year; 10.3 vs 18.3 rebalances per book. But 'does as well as' overstates: B beats Ac in-sample and in both halves for both tiers. The F3 gap of 0.027 is close to the per-half bar, and B's CAGR is higher (17.29% vs 16.83%; 20.88% vs 20.18%).
verdicts.corrected: Ac comes within 0.005 (F2) and 0.027 (F3) Calmar of B on the tranche, with B ahead in every half of both tiers, at about half the turnover (6.81 vs 12.87 F2; 6.89 vs 12.48 F3). It is within the rule's tolerance, not equal.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. Turnover B / A: F2 12.87 / 8.99, F3 12.48 / 8.70. A makes 35.0 vs 18.3 rebalances per book per year. Average leveraged-sleeve trade 12.8% vs 35.1% of book NAV (4.49/35.0 vs 6.44/18.3). H2 chop difference at 3/10/15 bps: F2 -0.012/-0.023/-0.031, F3 +0.007/-0.003/-0.010. Cross-market median: +0.0106 / +0.0019 / -0.0032. Labeling caveat: 'one-way' is common.py's sum of |dw| over all sleeves, which counts both legs. That is twice the standard one-way figure (F2 B is about 6.4 a year under the standard definition). Cost charging is internally consistent.

Every metric reproduces. Ulcer B/A 9.57/9.16 (F2), 13.59/13.46 (F3). Worst-5 mean -22.6/-21.8% and -28.9/-29.1%. CDaR95 -20.9/-20.3% and -26.5/-27.4%. B vs V: Ulcer 11.28 and 18.31; CDaR95 -28.4% and -41.5%; max drawdown -34.0% and -47.4%. 'No chop advantage' holds for F2, where B is slightly worse on all three shape metrics. For F3, B is better on CDaR95 (+0.9pp), worst-5 (+0.2pp) and max drawdown (-32.5% vs -35.3%), and worse only on Ulcer (by 0.13). The vol-target improvement also comes partly from 2001-02, not only 2000.
verdicts.corrected: At matched exposure the chop rule gives no drawdown-shape advantage for F2 and a small one for F3 (CDaR95 +0.9pp, max drawdown +2.8pp, Ulcer -0.13). The vol target improves every shape metric in-sample, mainly through 2000-02.

verdicts.reason: The seed-7 bootstrap reproduces exactly: chop F2 +0.086 (5th-95th percentile -0.047 to +0.233), P(<=0) 0.13; chop F3 +0.071, 0.11; vol F2 +0.039, 0.32; vol F3 +0.025, 0.42. Seeds 11, 123 and 2026 give P(<=0) of 0.13-0.15, 0.10-0.11, 0.30-0.32 and 0.38-0.42. IXIC -0.066 vs NDX-sim +0.054 is confirmed. Caveat: the bootstrap means for vol (+0.039, +0.025) are far below the point estimates (+0.119, +0.187), because resampling breaks up the 2000 drawdown. P(<=0) is therefore a percentile reading, not a null test. Information only.

F3 vol H2 is +0.03415. Re-matching exposure inside H2 gives +0.0291, which would fail. At 2x / vt .30 the target binds on 0.9% (spx) to 9.3% (hsi) of risk-on days, with c_V 0.9830-0.9992. In the 3x / vt .20 run it binds on 5.5-30.6%, with a vol median of +0.0122 (4 of 7 positive) and a chop median of -0.0007. A further knife edge: at 15 bps the H2 value is +0.03004.

The re-run reproduces all out-of-sample totals exactly. Tranche B/A/V: F2 -10.69/-8.55/-10.54%, F3 -14.91/-11.09/-13.83%. Friday: F2 -6.03/-1.77/-5.95%, F3 -8.99/-2.13/-7.65%. The window is 81 trading days (2026-07-27 to 2026-11-17). A lost less than B on every basis, and V was within 0.1-1.3pp of B.

Validation reproduced: numpy engine vs common.backtest differs by 0 (Friday) and at most 2.8e-17 (tranche); main_tranche_check is matched exactly; critic ablations agree to 4.6e-6 (F2 +0.0287, F3 +0.0715); rebuilt NDX signals differ on 0 days. My own checks agree. The rebuild through common.py of all 7 markets plus NDX, for B, A and V, matches to 5.6e-13. The truncated-panel run is identical. The yfinance cache matches another specialist's independent fetch (r2_friday_effect_yf.parquet): N225 and IXIC identical, DAX within 1.9e-5.

issues: No integrity defect found. Re-run: 0 differing leaves. Truncate-at-freeze rebuild: identical to 5.6e-13, so no post-freeze leakage. The spec-text weights match the specialist's engine. Weekday marks and tranche match main_tranche_check exactly. Costs match common.backtest. The vt_A solve agrees with an independent Illinois solver (0.117171, 0.116739, 0.108667, 0.108208).

Headline overstates: 'both components add Calmar only in NDX 1988-2006'. In 1990-2006, N225 has a chop difference of +0.198, and the vol-target difference is at least +0.03 in IXIC (+0.133), RUT (+0.039) and HSI (+0.033). 'The vol target only in the 2000 crash' is too narrow: the 2001-02 sub-period gives B minus V of +0.148 (F2) and +0.418 (F3).

The headline sentence 'Both components are de-levering dials, not sources of edge' goes further than the pre-registered verdicts. The F3 vol target is INCONCLUSIVE (retained by default) with H2 +0.034 above the bar; only 3 of the 4 verdicts are REPLACEABLE.

The F3 vol verdict is a knife edge. Its H2 margin over +0.03 is +0.0041 at 3 bps, +0.0012 at 10 bps and +0.00004 at 15 bps, and within-half re-matching (+0.0291) would flip it. It does not change with target- rather than held-weight exposure (+0.0341), with any pre-2000 gold treatment, or under truncation.

Turnover label: the 'annual one-way turnover' reported is common.py's sum of |dw| over all sleeves, which counts both legs. That is twice the standard one-way definition (F2 B about 6.4 a year, not 12.87). The cost model is consistent, so no number changes.

Shared-panel artifact, not the specialist's error: the panel's hsi differs from Yahoo ^HSI on 16 holiday-shifted days since 1990 (for example 1999-12-27/28). Using ^HSI gives an hsi chop difference of +0.0109 instead of +0.0106 and a median of +0.0109. No decision changes.

Gold before 2000-08-30 is used only as the constant 15% return sleeve, never as a signal, which is correct. It does carry intra-month look-ahead in its returns. Setting it to zero or to month-end lump returns moves the NDX H1 differences by at most 0.015 and the chop median by at most 0.0001 (to +0.0107 / +0.0106). All four decisions are unchanged.
The C4 single-weekday runs reuse the tranche-matched vt_A and c_V. Re-matching per book moves the values by at most 0.002, and Friday is still the most favourable weekday in all four cases.

Review scripts (they write only to the scratchpad; no other project file was modified): update_2026_11/r2_verify_chop_vol_matched_integrity_rerun.py, _checks.py (full and truncate modes), _sens.py and _episode.py.

verifications.lens: ROBUSTNESS (overfitting, period-boundary and single-episode dependence, bootstrap design, multiple testing, fragility of the pre-registered decisions)
verifications.rule_applied_correctly: Yes, applied exactly as written. decide() implements the rule as registered: RETAINED if the tranche Calmar difference is >= +0.03 in both 1988-01-01..2006-12-31 and 2007-01-01..2026-07-24 AND the 7-market median is >= +0.02. REPLACEABLE if the difference is < +0.03 in at least one half AND the median is <= +0.02. Anything else is INCONCLUSIVE. The settings also match the registration: tranche basis, 3 bps, lag 1, exposure matched over 1988-01-01..2026-07-24 per tier and basis (bisection error <= 2e-12), and a median over spx/rut/tsx/hsi/^GDAXI/^N225/^IXIC at 2x / vt .30 on the full 1990-01-01..2026-07-24 window, with NDX-sim excluded. The same 2x median is used for F3, as the registration says. Re-running r2_chop_vol_matched.py with its output redirected gave 0 numeric leaves different from the saved JSON. My separate numpy engine reproduces vtA, cV and every decision input to 3e-11. Outcomes as registered: chop F2 REPLACEABLE, chop F3 REPLACEABLE, vol F2 REPLACEABLE, vol F3 INCONCLUSIVE (retain by default). The outcomes are the same at 10 and 15 bps. FRAGILITY (information only; the rule as written governs): chop F2 and vol F2 do not change under any alternative I tried. Chop F3 flips only if 2022 is removed or on the Friday book. Vol F3 is the fragile one: it flips to REPLACEABLE under lag 2, under within-H2 re-matching, and when H2 starts in 2003, 2004 or 2005.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced bit-for-bit (re-run: 0 differing leaves; separate engine: 3e-11). At 3 bps: chop F2 H1 +0.2444 / H2 -0.0119; chop F3 +0.1554 / +0.0069; vol F2 +0.2485 / -0.0023; vol F3 +0.1587 / +0.0341. Medians are chop +0.0106 and vol -0.0005, giving REPLACEABLE / REPLACEABLE / REPLACEABLE / INCONCLUSIVE. At 10 / 15 bps the outcomes are the same (vol F3 H2 +0.0312 / +0.0300; medians -0.0008 / -0.0009). Fragility: chop F2 and vol F2 hold for every H2 start year 2003-2011, lag 2, volatility matching and a 1986 start (H2 ranges -0.044..+0.020 for chop and -0.006..+0.004 for vol). Chop F3 H2 stays between -0.011 and +0.025 except with 2022 removed (+0.070, which flips it to INCONCLUSIVE). Vol F3 flips to REPLACEABLE under lag 2 (H2 +0.029), within-H2 re-match (+0.029), and H2 start 2003 / 2004 / 2005 (+0.028 / +0.028 / +0.029). It stays INCONCLUSIVE for start years 2006-2011 (+0.032..+0.052).

The quoted numbers reproduce: NDX F2 1988-99 +0.436, 2000-12 -0.111, 2013-freeze -0.012; F3 +0.280 / +0.040 / +0.006; cross-market H1 median -0.117 (6 of 7 negative); H2 median +0.0096 (7 of 7 positive, maximum +0.055). But the 'one market' part is wrong, because the comparison mixes windows: NDX is quoted for 1988-99, while the other markets are quoted for 1990-2006, which nets their 1990s gains against their 2000-06 losses. On the same window, 1990-99, chop B minus A is SPX +0.261, RUT +0.353, N225 +0.266, IXIC +0.672. Re-matching exposure inside the decade gives +0.261 / +0.327 / +0.270 / +0.665. The 7-market 1990-99 median is +0.261, against NDX-F2 +0.370. In 2000-06 the difference is negative in 6 of 7 markets (median -0.254), and NDX-F2 is also negative (-0.129). NDX passes H1 mainly because of where the maximum drawdown falls: zeroing 1989-07..1990-12 cuts F2's H1 edge from +0.244 to +0.065.
verdicts.corrected: The chop rule's matched-exposure edge comes from one era, not one market. In 1990-99 it is about +0.26 to +0.67 in SPX, RUT, N225, IXIC and NDX (7-market median +0.261, robust to re-matching). It reverses in 2000-06 (median -0.254; NDX-F2 -0.129) and is about 0 since 2013 (median +0.023). NDX's H1 pass is mostly the 1989-90 drawdown.

verdicts.reason: Episode exclusion makes this stronger. Setting both legs to zero in Mar-Dec 2000 turns the vol in-sample Calmar difference from +0.119 to -0.013 (F2) and from +0.187 to -0.042 (F3). H1 goes from +0.248 to -0.040 (F2) and from +0.159 to -0.128 (F3). At matched exposure the vol target loses in 1988-99 (F2 -0.050, F3 -0.242). The binding rates (16.2 / 4.2% for F2, 42.9 / 22.8% for F3), the drawdown episodes (B -23.4% in 1989-10..1990-05; V -34.0% in 2000-03..2000-10; both -27.7% in 2021-11..2022-10) and the cross-market values all reproduce. One nuance: for F3, the H2 difference of +0.034 is not 'nothing'. It is the margin that makes F3 INCONCLUSIVE, and it survives removing 2022 (+0.034) or COVID (+0.041).

Friday has the largest difference in all four component-tier combinations. Chop F2: +0.218 vs next best +0.115. Chop F3: +0.237 vs +0.087. Vol F2: +0.244 vs +0.171. Vol F3: +0.256 vs +0.194. The Friday-book chop H2 values (+0.083 F2, +0.099 F3) and their flip to INCONCLUSIVE reproduce. The cross-market chop median on a Friday basis is -0.0145, so no Friday-specific cross-market support exists either.

The numbers reproduce: c = 0.715 / 0.719; Calmar 0.620 vs 0.625 (F2) and 0.616 vs 0.643 (F3); H1 / H2 +0.050 / +0.005 and +0.023 / +0.016; median +0.0052; turnover 6.81 vs 12.87; 10.3 vs 18.3 rebalances. But at 3 bps B is ahead of Ac in all four tranche tier-halves and in-sample (F2 +0.005, F3 +0.027). F2 H1 exceeds the bar (+0.050). On the Friday book B leads Ac by +0.160 (F2) and +0.106 (F3) in-sample. Ac pulls ahead only at 15 bps for F2 (0.576 vs 0.549). F3 at 15 bps is a tie (0.573 vs 0.573), and on the Friday book B still leads by +0.099 / +0.072 at 15 bps.
verdicts.corrected: Ac comes within 0.03 Calmar of B on the tranche in 3 of 4 tier-halves, but B is slightly ahead in all four at 3 bps. With half the turnover, Ac wins only for F2 at 15 bps.

verdicts.reason: Turnover a year, B / A: 12.87 / 8.99 (F2) and 12.48 / 8.70 (F3). Rebalances per book: 35.0 vs 18.3. Average leveraged-sleeve trade, recomputed: A 4.49 / 35.0 = 12.8% of NAV; B 6.44 / 18.3 = 35.1%. H2 chop difference at 3 / 10 / 15 bps: F2 -0.012 / -0.023 / -0.031; F3 +0.007 / -0.003 / -0.010. Cross-market median: +0.0106 / +0.0019 / -0.0032.

All values reproduce: Ulcer 9.57 / 9.16 / 11.28 (F2) and 13.59 / 13.46 / 18.31 (F3); CDaR95 -20.9 / -20.3 / -28.4 and -26.5 / -27.4 / -41.5; worst-5 mean -22.6 / -21.8 and -28.9 / -29.1. 'Mainly because of 2000' is in fact 'entirely'. With 2000-02 set to zero for both legs, B vs V becomes: F2 Ulcer 8.72 vs 8.60, CDaR -19.9 vs -19.8, max drawdown -27.7 vs -27.7; F3 Ulcer 12.97 vs 12.43, CDaR -26.5 vs -26.2, max drawdown -32.5 vs -32.8. The no-vol version is then equal or slightly better.

The figures reproduce exactly (seed 7, 63-day blocks): chop F2 +0.086 (-0.047..+0.233, P 0.13); chop F3 P 0.11; vol F2 P 0.32; vol F3 P 0.42. But the bootstrap is strongly biased. Bootstrap mean minus point estimate: chop F2 +0.031, chop F3 -0.048, vol F2 -0.080, vol F3 -0.162. 90-97% of vol draws fall below the observed value, and the vol F3 5-95% band (-0.075..+0.156) excludes its own point estimate (+0.187). So P(<=0) is not a valid test here, and it depends on block length: vol F3 0.42 (63-day) falls to 0.20 (504-day), and chop F3 0.11 falls to 0.06. A bias-corrected (basic) bootstrap gives p = 0.000-0.026 for vol F2, vol F3 and chop F3 at 21-252-day blocks. The bootstrap therefore neither supports nor rules out 'noise'. The robust statement is episode dependence, shown in C3 and C2.
verdicts.corrected: The 63-day block bootstrap is too biased for this Calmar statistic to settle significance. Episode-exclusion tests show the in-sample differences come from single episodes or eras: 2000 for the vol target, 1989-90 and the 1990s for the chop rule.

verdicts.reason: F3 H2 +0.0341; within-H2 re-match +0.0291; target active 0.9-9.3% of risk-on days in the 7 markets; c = 0.983-0.9992; 3x / vt .20 information run: vol median +0.0122 (4 of 7), chop -0.0007, target active 5.5-30.6%. Further evidence of the knife edge: lag 2 gives H2 +0.029 (REPLACEABLE), and H2 starts of 2003-2005 give +0.028-0.029. The cross-market vol median stays between -0.0022 and -0.0003 under all 5 constructions I tried, so RETAINED is effectively unreachable.

Out-of-sample totals reproduce: B / A / V F2 tranche -10.69 / -8.55 / -10.54%; F3 tranche -14.91 / -11.09 / -13.83%; F2 Friday -6.03 / -1.77 / -5.95%; F3 Friday -8.99 / -2.13 / -7.65%. The window has 81 trading days (2026-07-27..2026-11-17).

The re-run is identical (0 differing leaves). My engine matches main_tranche_check (Calmar difference < 1e-12) and the specialist's vtA, cV and Calmar differences to 3e-11. The rebuilt cross-market medians match exactly (+0.01056 / -0.00053). The specialist's checks against the critic's numbers (4.6e-6) and common.py (2.8e-17) are in the re-run log.

issues: C2's 'one market' framing does not hold. It compares NDX in 1988-99 with other markets in 1990-2006. On the same 1990-99 window, the matched chop edge is +0.26 to +0.67 in SPX, RUT, N225 and IXIC (7-market median +0.261, unchanged by re-matching inside the decade). It is negative in 2000-06 in 6 of 7 markets (median -0.254) and for NDX-F2 (-0.129). This is an era effect across markets. NDX's H1 pass is mostly the 1989-90 drawdown: zeroing 1989-07..1990-12 cuts F2 H1 from +0.244 to +0.065.

The vol F3 INCONCLUSIVE verdict is fragile. It flips to REPLACEABLE under lag 2 (H2 +0.029; common.py's conservative execution check), under within-H2 re-matching (+0.029), and with H2 starting in 2003 / 2004 / 2005 (+0.028 / +0.028 / +0.029). Its H1 leg is entirely the 2000 episode: H1 becomes -0.128 with Mar-Dec 2000 set to zero. The rule as written still governs, so INCONCLUSIVE (retain by default) stands.

Chop F3 REPLACEABLE depends on a single H2 episode. Zeroing 2022 raises H2 from +0.007 to +0.070, which would make it INCONCLUSIVE. Both chop verdicts also flip on the Friday book (H2 +0.083 / +0.099), as the specialist reported.

Robust parts: chop F2 and vol F2 REPLACEABLE hold for H2 start years 2003-2011 (9 of 9), lag 2, realised-volatility matching (chop F2 H2 -0.044, vol F2 +0.004) and a 1986-07 start that adds 1987 (H1 moves by <= 0.009; Q4-1987 F2 B -6.2%, A -8.2%, V -5.9%). The cross-market chop median stays <= +0.02 under every alternative construction: registered +0.0106, lag 2 +0.0053, volatility-matched +0.0164, Friday basis -0.0145, 1988 start +0.0046. The vol median stays between -0.0022 and -0.0003.

Bootstrap design flaw (C8): the 63-day block bootstrap of the Calmar difference is badly biased (mean minus point estimate = -0.080 for vol F2, -0.162 for vol F3), and the vol F3 5-95% band excludes its own estimate. P(<=0) shifts with block length (vol F3 from 0.42 to 0.20, chop F3 from 0.11 to 0.06 at 504 days). A bias-corrected bootstrap gives p <= 0.026 for vol F2, vol F3 and chop F3. 'Cannot be told apart from noise' is not established by this tool.

The headline overreaches. 'Both components are de-levering dials, not sources of edge' is stronger than the registered result for vol F3, which is INCONCLUSIVE (retain by default). The evidence supports 'the vol target's in-sample value is a single episode (2000)', not a rule-based verdict of REPLACEABLE for F3.

The recommendation's 'practical payoff' from replacing the chop rule with a constant 0.71x multiplier rests only on F2 tranche at 15 bps (0.576 vs 0.549). F3 at 15 bps is a tie (0.573 vs 0.573). At 3 bps B beats Ac in all four tranche tier-halves (+0.050 / +0.005 / +0.023 / +0.016). On the Friday book B leads by +0.07 to +0.16 in-sample at every cost. The specialist correctly requires a separate pre-registered test before adoption.

Calmar per half is set by one or two drawdowns, so the halves are effectively small samples. Setting Mar-Dec 2000 to zero changes the vol in-sample difference from +0.119 to -0.013 (F2) and from +0.187 to -0.042 (F3). With 2000-02 removed, the vol target's Ulcer and CDaR advantage disappears entirely (F2 Ulcer 8.72 vs 8.60; F3 12.97 vs 12.43). At matched exposure the vol target loses in 1988-99 (F2 -0.050, F3 -0.242).

No hidden selection found. Every computed variant is in the JSON, and the variant count of 157 is accurate (127 return-evaluated + 30 per-weekday). This review evaluated 138 more information-only strategy variants, none of which affects a decision. Scripts (outputs written only to the scratchpad): update_2026_11/r2_verify_chop_vol_matched_robustness_rerun.py, ..._checks.py, ..._followup.py, ..._era.py, ..._lib.py (the last four share the same folder and prefix r2_verify_chop_vol_matched_robustness_).

dims.title: Final candidate comparison on the timing-luck-free basis with implementation costs
dims.task: FINAL CANDIDATE TABLE (no selection - every config is fixed here). Tiers F1 (qqq vt .20), F2 (qld vt .30), F3 (tqqq vt .20); off-leg {IEF; 50/50 IEF+bills via off_weights}; gold_phys 15%. Bases: (i) Friday book (July convention, lag 1, 3 bps); (ii) 5-weekday tranche, lag 1, 3 bps; (iii) US realistic = tranche, lag 1, 5 bps; (iv) UCITS proxy = tranche, lag 2, 15 bps on the Nasdaq sleeve and 8 bps on IEF/bills/gold (write a per-sleeve-cost backtest; it must reproduce common.backtest exactly when costs are equal). Periods: 1988-01-01..2026-07-24, 2000-01-01..2026-07-24, 2007-01-01..2026-07-24, and OOS 2026-07-25..end (reported separately). Metrics: CAGR, maxDD, Calmar, Sharpe on EXCESS returns (r - rf_d), Ulcer index, mean of 5 worst drawdowns, CDaR95, worst 12-month return, % negative calendar years. Benchmarks: QQQ buy-and-hold, 60/40 (spx/ief), static 85% IEF + 15% gold_phys. Statistics: stationary (Politis-Romano) block bootstrap with mean block lengths 126 and 252 days, at least 2,000 reps, for: each candidate minus QQQ (CAGR, Calmar, Ulcer differences), F2 minus F3, F2 minus F1, and 50/50 vs IEF within each tier; report 95% CIs and P(diff <= 0). Also REPRODUCE OR REFUTE the critic's unreviewed numbers in update_2026_11/critic_out_critic_candidates.json (e.g. F2 tranche 17.3%/-27.7%/0.62; since-2000 13.4%/0.48; F1 UCITS-proxy 10.2%/-21.3%/0.48 with Calmar edge vs QQQ +0.33 [+0.03, +0.73]; F2 UCITS-proxy edge vs QQQ Calmar +0.22 [-0.05, +0.54]). Conclude with a planning table: per tier and route (US, UCITS), the expected CAGR / maxDD / Calmar range to plan on, explicitly NOT using the Friday premium.

result.dimension: candidates_tranche: final candidate comparison on the timing-luck-free basis, with implementation costs
result.headline: Planning numbers without timing luck (5-weekday tranche; in-sample 1988 to 2026-07-24; ranges cover 1988, 2000 and 2007 starts). US ETFs: F1 9.1-10.6% CAGR, -20.9% maxDD, Calmar 0.44-0.51. F2 13.1-17.0%, -27.8% (1-in-20: -36.7%), Calmar 0.47-0.61. F3 16.7-21.6%, -32.6% (1-in-20: -46.0%), Calmar 0.53-0.68. The UCITS proxy costs about 1pp/yr more. Every critic number reproduces exactly. Its claim that only F1 survives UCITS costs does not hold: it comes from the 63-day bootstrap. With 126- and 252-day stationary blocks, all three tiers' Calmar edges over QQQ are borderline for 1988-2026 (P 0.02-0.06), and none is significant from 2007.
decisions: Pre-registered everything in the script docstring before computing: 6 configs (F1/F2/F3 x IEF or 50/50 IEF+bills, 15% gold_phys) x 4 bases = 24 candidates. Nothing was selected or tuned.

Bases: Friday book = P.mark, lag 1, 3bp. Tranche = equal-weight mean of the Mon..Fri books, lag 1, 3bp. US = tranche, lag 1, 5bp. UCITS proxy = tranche, lag 2, 15bp on the Nasdaq sleeve and 8bp on IEF/bills/gold.
Applied the 15bp UCITS cost to every tier's Nasdaq sleeve, F1's QQQ included, as the spec says. The critic used 8bp for F1.
Per-sleeve cost backtest (backtest_ps) groups sleeves by cost level in column order, so with equal costs it runs exactly common.backtest's arithmetic.
Primary window IS88 (1988-01-01..2026-07-24); IS00 and IS07 are supplementary. OOS (2026-07-25..2026-11-17, 81 days) is reported separately as totals and informs no decision.
Benchmarks: QQQ = P.qqq. 60/40 (spx/ief) and 85% IEF + 15% gold are daily constant mixes with no costs.

Kept the 60/40 on the panel's price-only SPX. Fetching ^SP500TR failed because the sandbox has no network, so I deleted my own failed helper r2_candidates_tranche_fetch.py. The only files written are r2_candidates_tranche.py and r2_candidates_tranche.json.

Stationary bootstrap (Politis-Romano: geometric block lengths, circular wrap), mean blocks 126 and 252, 5,000 paired reps per window and block length. Fixed seeds: 137/263 (IS88), 148/274 (IS00), 159/285 (IS07). Percentile 95% CIs; P(diff<=0) = share of resamples.
Pairs: each of the 24 candidates minus QQQ; F2 minus F3 and F2 minus F1 per off-leg and basis; 50/50 minus IEF per tier and basis. Metrics: CAGR, Calmar, Ulcer, plus excess Sharpe.

Planning rule, fixed in advance: CAGR and Calmar range = min..max of the IS88/IS00/IS07 point estimates on the route basis (US = 'us', UCITS = 'ucits'). maxDD = realized IS88 value plus the bootstrap median and 5th percentile (L=252, IS88). No Friday-basis number is used.

Critic check: rebuilt all 9 critic specs in my own engine and re-ran its exact 63-day circular bootstrap (seed 0, 2,000 reps). Also ran its F1 8/8bp tranche series through the stationary bootstrap, as a reproduction-only series (not a candidate).

result.recommendation:
1. Plan on the PLAN rows (tranche basis), never on the Friday book.
   - US route, IEF off-leg:
     - F1: CAGR 9.1-10.6%, Calmar 0.44-0.51, maxDD about -18% typical and -24% in a 1-in-20 case (realized -21%).
     - F2: CAGR 13.1-17.0%, Calmar 0.47-0.61, maxDD -28% typical and -37% in a 1-in-20 case.
     - F3: CAGR 16.7-21.6%, Calmar 0.53-0.68, maxDD -36% typical and -46% in a 1-in-20 case (realized -33%).
   - UCITS route: about 1pp/yr less CAGR and 0.05-0.07 less Calmar (F1 8.3-9.7%, F2 12.4-15.9%). F3 has no viable UCITS product. Round 1 measured real UCITS gaps of 2.1-3.2%/yr, against about 1.1pp in this proxy, so plan at the bottom of the UCITS range.
   - Treat the Friday premium as unplanned upside: +1.0pp (F1), +2.4pp (F2), +3.3pp/yr (F3), and only about half that with a one-session delay.

2. Choose the tier by the drawdown you can tolerate, not by efficiency. F1, F2 and F3 tie on excess Sharpe and Calmar (P(diff<=0) 0.24-0.67). Each step up adds 3.6-6.4pp/yr of CAGR and 4-5 Ulcer points.

3. Keep IEF as the default off-leg. The 50/50 IEF/bills split insures against a 2022-type stock-and-bond selloff for about 1pp/yr, with significantly lower excess Sharpe for F2 and F3. It is easiest to justify for F1 (1-in-20 maxDD -17.8% vs -23.7%). If you choose it, decide on regime grounds, not on its in-sample Calmar.

4. Describe the edge over QQQ as avoiding drawdowns (Ulcer 4.5-13.7 vs 36.8), not as extra return:
   - No tier has a significant CAGR edge; F3's is borderline (P 0.05).
   - The Calmar edge is borderline for 1988-2026, significant from 2000, and not significant from 2007.
   - If the next few years look like 2010-2026, expect to roughly match QQQ's return with about half its drawdown, not to beat it.

5. The critic's numbers can be quoted as computed. Drop its conclusion that F1 is the only tier whose edge survives UCITS costs: that comes from the 63-day bootstrap.
caveats: The 60/40 benchmark uses the panel's price-only S&P 500 (1988-2025 CAGR 9.1%), so it leaves out dividends and is understated by roughly 1pp/yr. A total-return fetch (^SP500TR) failed because the sandbox has no network.

Before each ETF's inception the sleeves are simulated:
- QQQ before 1999: NDX price minus 0.20%/yr, no dividends.
- QLD/TQQQ: 2x/3x NDX minus 0.95% minus financing at the T-bill rate.
- IEF/TLT before 2002: calibrated synthetics; bills before 2007: T-bill minus 0.13%.
- gold_phys before 2000-08-30: a monthly-average interpolation, used only as a return sleeve, never as a signal.
Round 1 judged the 3x simulation 0.2-0.5pp/yr optimistic in high-rate eras.

The UCITS proxy models only trading costs and a one-session delay, on US data. It leaves out product-level differences (TER, swap costs) and European-close timing noise. Round 1 measured real UCITS-route gaps of 2.1-3.2%/yr on one Monday draw (1.0-2.25 on Tuesday or Wednesday), against about 1.1pp here. F3 UCITS rows are hypothetical.

Rule flaws I applied anyway, as instructed:
- 15bp on the 1x sleeve is probably conservative for a liquid 1x UCITS fund; at 8bp F1 UCITS gains 0.48pp/yr.
- A planning range taken as min-max over nested windows understates sampling uncertainty (bootstrap 5-95% CAGR for F2 US: 12.2-22.3%).
- F2's bootstrap median maxDD is anchored on the single 2022 episode.

Bootstrap P(diff<=0) is the share of resamples, not a p-value. The 24 candidate-vs-QQQ tests are not adjusted for multiplicity. Calmar-difference distributions are off-centre in tier-dependent directions (claim C15), so percentile CIs are only approximate.
Bootstrap maxDD figures apply to a 38.5-year horizon; over shorter horizons the typical maxDD is milder.

The tranche is the daily-rebalanced average of five weekday books, the constant-mix convention used elsewhere in this research. Run live as five sub-accounts, the books would drift slightly apart and need five times as many orders.

The planning ranges exclude three further drags: a parameter-selection haircut (the critic, unreviewed, puts the defaults at about the 82nd-84th percentile of the tranche grid), taxes and withholding, and US estate-tax exposure.

Variants: 34 distinct configurations were evaluated: 24 pre-registered candidates, 3 benchmarks and 7 reproduction-only critic series. On top of those, 90 single-weekday component books are reported, and 11 critic series came out identical to candidates. Nothing was selected.
The OOS window is only 81 trading days, so only total returns are quoted; annualised OOS figures in the JSON are not meaningful.
Runtime is 457 s, close to the 540 s timeout used for these runs; a re-run on a slower machine could time out.

dims.title: Diagnosis of the Friday rebalance premium
dims.task: DIAGNOSE THE FRIDAY PREMIUM. (a) Reproduce the five weekday books and the tranche for F1/F2/F3-IEF; decompose the Friday-minus-tranche gap by decade and by calendar year, and by event type: weeks where the Friday book switched risk-on/off vs weeks with only size changes vs no change. Which episodes/years contribute most? (b) NDX day-of-week mean returns, volatility and Monday-gap (Friday close to Monday open is not available - use close-to-close Monday returns) by era (1985-1999, 2000-2009, 2010-2026); does a weekend/Monday effect mechanically favour Friday-close decisions for a trend gate? Test whether the premium is explained by the first holding day after each decision. (c) Cross-market replication with the F2 rules (2x sim sleeve 2*r - 0.95%/252 - rf_d, own-price signals, IEF + 15% gold_phys, vt .30) on S&P 500, Russell 2000, TSX, Hang Seng (panel returns), DAX (^GDAXI), Nikkei (^N225), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC, 1971+; use 1975+): which weekday wins in each market and each half? (d) Placebo: 1,000 random rebalance-day schedules (one random weekday drawn independently each week) - where does the Friday book's Calmar and CAGR fall in that distribution, in-sample and in each half? (e) Check for mechanical/data artifacts: Yahoo ^NDX history quality 1985-1990 (stale or duplicated closes, missing days), holiday-week handling, the July 'mark' definition. CONCLUDE: is there evidence (holding in both halves AND in other markets) that Friday rebalancing is structurally better? If not, the planning basis is the tranche and the Friday premium is luck to be treated as upside. Recommend which day the live automation should use (note: a fixed day is required operationally; the question is only what to EXPECT).

result.dimension: Diagnosis of the Friday rebalance premium (KEY = friday_effect)
result.headline: Applying the pre-registered rule, Friday rebalancing is NOT structurally better. Criterion A passes: on NDX, F2 Friday beats the 5-weekday tranche in both halves (H1 +2.92pp CAGR / +0.19 Calmar, H2 +1.95pp / +0.18) and sits at the 99.3rd and 99.6th percentile of a 1,000-schedule placebo. Criterion B fails: Friday beats the tranche on both CAGR and Calmar in only 3 of 7 other markets (5 needed); SPX Friday ranks last in both halves. The first holding day does not explain the premium overall. It explains H1, an expired Friday-to-Monday continuation in stale Nasdaq closes (Fri-to-Mon correlation +0.25 in 1988-99, 0.00 since 2007), but not H2. The premium's size also peaks at the EMA-100 length that was tuned on Friday backtests. Plan on the tranche (F2 in-sample 17.29% / -27.7% / Calmar 0.62; a single fixed day has a median maxDD of about -29.5%) and treat Friday's 19.71% / -24.0% / 0.82 as upside. Keep Friday as the live day, and do not use Monday-close decisions.
decisions: Decision rule fixed in the script docstring before any round-2 number was computed. STRUCTURAL iff A and B. A: on NDX F2-IEF, Friday minus tranche > 0 in both CAGR and Calmar in H1 (1988-01-01..2006-12-31) and H2 (2007-01-01..2026-07-24), AND Friday's Calmar >= 95th percentile of the 1,000-schedule random-weekday placebo in both halves. B: under the F2 rules, Friday minus tranche > 0 in both CAGR and Calmar in >= 5 of 7 other markets (SPX, RUT, TSX, HSI from panel returns; DAX, N225, IXIC on their own calendars).

Rule applied exactly as written: A = true, B = false (3/7), so not structural. Planning basis = 5-weekday tranche; the Friday premium = luck, treated as upside. F1/F3, OOS and all other numbers are reported only.

Diagnostic (b), also fixed in advance: the first holding day explains the premium iff (i) lag 2 removes >= 2/3 of the in-sample gap AND (ii) >= 2/3 of the arithmetic gap is earned on the first session after Friday decisions. F2 result: false (53% and 24%).

Placebo: one weekday drawn independently per W-FRI week; if that weekday is a holiday the week is skipped (same holiday handling as the fixed-weekday books); 1,000 draws; seed 20261118 for F2, fixed offsets for the others. Secondary null: one weekday per 13-week block, which keeps regular spacing.

Cross-market windows: panel markets from max(1988-01-01, first data + 250 sessions) (RUT from 1988-09-07); DAX from 1988-12-28; IXIC and N225 from 1975-01-01. Halves split at each market's window midpoint. IXIC is also reported for 1975-1987 (before the NDX sample).

Own-calendar off-leg: panel IEF and gold_phys mapped as-of onto each calendar. Before 1985-10-02, IEF is rebuilt from ^TNX with the recovered panel calibration (alpha 0.305%/yr, duration 7.09, convexity 76.9; correlation 1.0 with the panel synthetic) and gold is replaced by T-bills. rf = panel rf (^IRX before the panel). 2x sleeve = 2r - 0.95%/252 - rf_d.

Event decomposition: each in-sample day is assigned to the Friday decision whose lag-1 holding window contains it. Decision classes: switch on/off (near-EMA <1% or far), size-only, stay-off, stay-on-same-size. Also split by whether the 5 books agree on risk state, and by disagreement episodes (maximal runs of disagreement days).

Added after the first run, diagnostics only, nothing selected: EMA-span grid {50,75,100,125,150,200,250}; 45-config vt x chop sub-grid at EMA-100; per-market lag-2 test and next-session autocorrelation; 13-week-null maxDD; options-expiry t-test; sensitivity of criterion B.
Live day recommendation: keep Friday close as the fixed day; set expectations from the tranche and the single-day timing-luck distribution, not from the Friday book.

claims.claim: Pre-registered verdict: A passes, B fails, so Friday rebalancing is not structurally better and the planning basis is the 5-weekday tranche.

B: Friday beats the tranche on both metrics in 3/7 markets: RUT +0.33pp / +0.0001 (knife-edge), N225 +1.47 / +0.045, IXIC +1.69 / +0.092. It fails in SPX (-0.72 / -0.098), TSX (-0.56 / +0.008), HSI (-0.20 / -0.023) and DAX (-0.12 / +0.005). 5 needed.

claims.claim: The premium is episodic. It comes almost entirely from Friday being invested while some other weekday books are out, and a few years carry most of it.
claims.evidence: F2 in-sample arithmetic gap 2.11pp/yr. 80% of it (1.69pp/yr) accrues on the 14% of days (1,374/9,712) when the 5 books disagree on risk state. 74% (+1.57pp/yr) comes on days Friday is in and another book is out; only 6% (+0.12) when Friday is out. 216 disagreement episodes, Friday ahead in 135; top 10 = 49% of the gap, top 20 = 79%. Largest: 2025-05-05..14 +5.97pp (tariff rebound), 1988-01-07..14 +4.79, 1998-06-16..22 +4.38, 2002-10-28..11-07 +4.27. Worst: 1997-04-24..05-02 -6.02. Friday ahead in 29/39 years (H1 13/19, H2 16/20); 1998 alone +31.4pp; the top 5 years (1998, 2018, 2012, 2006, 1991) = 59% of the log gap. Dropping the top 3 years cuts the mean annual gap from 2.81 to 1.57pp.

claims.claim: By the Friday book's decision type, size-change weeks and switch weeks carry the premium; no-change weeks carry almost none.
claims.evidence: F2 in-sample, 2.11pp/yr gap. Switch weeks (189, 10% of weeks): +0.90pp/yr (43%), of which near-EMA (<1%) switches (75 weeks) +0.46 (22%). Size-only weeks (517): +1.14 (54%). No-change weeks (1,238): +0.07 (3%). H1 switch/size/none: +1.25/+1.68/-0.40; H2: +0.56/+0.61/+0.54. By sleeve: QLD +2.22, IEF -0.11, costs +0.01pp/yr. Friday has fewer on/off switches than the other books (189 vs 214-217).

claims.claim: The first holding day does not explain the premium overall. It explains the H1 part completely and the H2 part not at all.
claims.evidence: Pre-registered diagnostic fails for F2: lag 2 removes 53% of the in-sample gap (+2.43 to +1.15pp; >= 67% needed), and only 24% of the arithmetic gap is earned on the first session after a Friday decision. H1: gap +2.92 to -0.09pp at lag 2 (103% removed; Monday carries 52%). H2: gap +1.95 to +2.34pp at lag 2 (it grows); it is earned on Wednesdays (+0.81) and Thursdays (+1.06pp/yr), with Monday -0.20. F3 shows the same split (H1 +4.08 to -0.07; H2 +2.43 to +3.30).

claims.claim: The H1 mechanism was real but has expired: Friday moves continued on Monday because Nasdaq closing prices were stale.
claims.evidence: NDX Friday-to-next-session return correlation: 1988-99 +0.25 (Spearman +0.30) vs -0.19..+0.05 for the other weekdays; 2000-06 +0.01; 2007-26 +0.00. SPX 1988-99 +0.07. IXIC 1975-87 +0.50. NDX daily autocorrelation 1985-89 +0.18, and NDX leads IXIC by a day (correlation 0.32). Friday switch-offs were followed by Mondays averaging -71bp in H1 (n=49) but +1bp in H2 (n=45). The H1 Friday premiums in HSI, DAX, N225 and IXIC also disappear at lag 2.

claims.claim: No weekend or Monday mean effect mechanically favours Friday-close decisions.
claims.evidence: Exact split of the F2 in-sample gap: mean channel (average exposure difference x average return) -0.03pp/yr vs timing channel +2.14pp/yr. Every book holds the same average exposure on each weekday, so a Monday mean cannot favour any of them. NDX Monday mean (close-to-close): 1985-99 -0.3bp/day (Monday minus rest -13.7bp, t -2.0, variance 1.43x); 2000-09 -8.7bp (t -0.9, variance 1.00x); 2010-26 +10.8bp (t +2.3, Monday minus rest +4.2bp). The sign flips across eras.

claims.claim: Post-hoc, not pre-registered: across markets the robust pattern is a Monday-close penalty, not a Friday premium.
claims.evidence: Monday is the worst Calmar book in 6/7 other markets (RUT, TSX, HSI, DAX, N225, IXIC) and on NDX. Monday Calmar placebo percentiles: NDX F2 4.1, IXIC 1.3, HSI 5.7, N225 7.6, RUT 7.9, DAX 14.6. Monday ranks last in all 45 in-sample vt x chop configurations at EMA-100. NDX Monday switch-offs were followed by Tuesday rebounds of +68bp (H1, n=59) and +83bp (H2, n=49). Friday is the best Calmar book in-sample only in DAX and N225; SPX Friday ranks 5th in-sample and in both halves.

claims.claim: Post-hoc: the premium's size is tied to the EMA length that was chosen on Friday-rebalanced backtests.
claims.evidence: F2 Friday minus tranche, EMA span 50/75/100/125/150/200/250: CAGR +1.14/+2.17/+2.43/+1.16/+0.87/+0.36/-0.02pp; Calmar -0.002/+0.178/+0.198/+0.002/+0.003/+0.082/+0.079. EMA-100 (the July pick from a 100-250 grid run on Friday rebalancing) gives the largest premium. The median across spans is +1.14pp / +0.079 Calmar; in H2 it is +0.46pp vs +1.95 at EMA-100. At EMA-100 the vt x chop sub-grid keeps Friday ahead in 45/45 in-sample configurations (median +1.87pp).

claims.claim: No data or mechanical artifact explains the premium.
claims.evidence: The NDX calendar is identical to ^GSPC since 1985-10-02 (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 weekend rows). Only 2 zero-return days in 1985-90, none on a Friday. No timestamp shift: same-day correlation with ^IXIC 0.94-0.99, one-day lead/lag <= 0.32. P.mark = trading Fridays = engine.py W-FRI rule (the July definition); mark_wk = last trading day of each week. Substituting holidays leaves the gap at +2.42pp (vs +2.43); there are 68 Friday-holiday weeks in-sample (Monday 183). Options-expiry Fridays carry 39% of the gap on 23% of weeks, but the difference is not significant (t 1.12). The 1985-99 NDX Wednesday mean (+32bp/day, t 6.5) also appears in IXIC and SPX, so it is a market feature, not an NDX data error. Yahoo NDX opens equal the prior close on 77-99% of days in 1985-98, so a Monday-open test is impossible.

claims.claim: What to expect from a single fixed rebalance day.
claims.evidence: F2 in-sample: tranche 17.29% / -27.7% / 0.62 (H1 18.03%, H2 16.59%). Single regular weekly schedule (13-week-block null): CAGR median 17.15% (5-95% range 15.5-18.8%), maxDD median -29.5% (5th percentile -34.4%), Calmar median 0.58. Friday's 19.71 / -24.0 / 0.82 is a 99.5th / 99.9th percentile outcome. F3: tranche 20.88 / -32.5 / 0.64, single-day median maxDD -37.1% (per-week null). F1: tranche 10.90 / -20.8 / 0.52.

claims.claim: Out-of-sample (2026-07-27..11-17, not used for any decision), Friday again did best, but within the range of luck.
claims.evidence: F2: Friday -6.03% vs tranche -10.69% (Mon -9.38, Tue -13.19, Wed -12.90, Thu -12.22). Friday is at the 90.5th percentile of 1,000 random schedules (median -11.8%). F3: -8.99 vs -14.91 (92.4th percentile). F1: -4.41 vs -6.61 (90.7th). The ordering rests on 2 whipsaw events.

result.recommendation: Keep the Friday close (market-on-close) as the fixed rebalance day for the live automation. The rulebook, the scanner and every reported number use it. No other weekday is shown to be better. The only cross-market regularity found (post-hoc) is that Monday-close decisions are the worst, so do not move decisions to Monday's close. Set expectations from the tranche, not from the Friday book. For F2 in-sample that means about 17.3% CAGR and a maxDD of about -28% on the tranche. A single fixed day has a median maxDD of about -29.5% and a 5th percentile of about -34%. F3: about 20.9% CAGR, tranche maxDD -32.5%, single-day median about -37%. Treat the Friday backtest's extra ~2.4pp/yr and ~4pp shallower drawdown as upside that cannot be counted on. Its H1 source (Friday-to-Monday continuation from stale Nasdaq closes) disappeared after 2000. Its H2 source has no established mechanism, appears only on NDX, and is tied to the tuned EMA length. Holiday handling is immaterial: skipping a holiday-Friday week and trading the week's last session give the same results.
caveats: The criterion-B threshold (5 of 7) and the market set are judgement calls, but the result holds under every reading tried: 3/7 as specified, 4/7 with HSI on its own calendar, 4/7 in H1, 3/7 in H2, and Friday best by Calmar in only 2/7. RUT's pass rests on a +0.0001 Calmar difference; counting it as a fail gives 2/7.

Separate view on the rule (applied unchanged above). B treats a possibly Nasdaq-specific microstructure effect as non-structural: IXIC 1975-87, before the NDX sample, also has Friday best (98th placebo percentile, Fri-to-Mon correlation +0.50). A is partly inflated because EMA-100 was tuned on Friday-rebalanced backtests (C10). Neither point supports expecting a forward Friday premium, because the H1 mechanism has gone (Fri-to-Mon correlation 0.00 since 2007).
IXIC overlaps NDX (same-day correlation 0.94-0.99 since 1985), so after 1985 it is not an independent replication.

Cross-market sleeves are simulated 2x on price indices with no dividends and US T-bill financing. Before 1985-10-02, IEF is rebuilt from ^TNX and gold is replaced by T-bills; gold is a constant 15% sleeve, so it cannot favour a weekday. Foreign calendars use as-of mapping of the US sleeves. N225 in the 1970s has 3.5% zero-return days.

The per-week placebo spaces rebalances irregularly, which makes it about 0.6pp CAGR too pessimistic (mean 16.54% vs 17.15% for the 13-week-block null). Planning numbers use the block null; Friday stays at the 95.6-99.9th percentile under it.

Several diagnostics were added after the first run and were not pre-registered: the EMA/vt/chop grid, the per-market lag-2 and autocorrelation tests, the block-null maxDD, the options-expiry t-test, the criterion-B sensitivity and the Monday observations. Nothing was selected from them.

No intraday data, so the 15:45 ET pre-close MOC approximation cannot be tested. Yahoo NDX opens before about 1999 are synthetic (equal to the prior close), so Friday-close to Monday-open returns cannot be measured; Monday returns are close-to-close.
maxDD is a single-path statistic, so Calmar comparisons between books inherit that fragility.
The OOS window is 81 trading days containing 2 whipsaw events; it was not used for any decision.
Variant count 13,409: 409 strategy books (including 260 grid books) plus 13,000 placebo schedules.

issues: Reproduction is exact. update_2026_11/r2_verify_friday_effect_integrity_rerun.py re-executes the unchanged script source and finds 0 numeric diffs. Independent pandas/common.py paths reproduce all three tiers, the placebo (same seed) and all 8 cross-market rows (criterion B = 3/7).

No look-ahead found. Signals use the close at t and weights apply from t+1. Gold, including the pre-2000 monthly interpolation, is only a constant 15% sleeve identical in every book and never a signal. OOS data never enters in-sample statistics. The Aug-Sep seasonal-boundary windows contribute -0.01pp/yr in-sample.

Minor post-freeze leakage into a deciding input. The pre-1985 IEF rebuild (used for N225 and IXIC, both counted in B) uses the shared panel's calibration fit on real IEF to 2026-11-17. A fit on data to 2026-07-24 only (alpha 0.273% / duration 7.094 / convexity 86.4 vs 0.305% / 7.091 / 76.9) moves N225 and IXIC by <0.004pp CAGR and <0.001 Calmar. Immaterial.

C6/C7 mechanism story is partly wrong. The first-day mechanism covers 1988-99 only: 1988-94 is generic index staleness (all-day AC1 +0.13, first-day share 39%); 1995-99 is a Friday-only continuation (all-day AC1 -0.04) carried by 5 crash Mondays. The 2000-06 part of H1 (+2.75pp) is unexplained (lag 2 removes 41%, first-day share -7%). H1 as a whole fails the pre-registered criterion (ii) at 52%.

Placebo null bias. The per-week null used in rule A rates any regular schedule highly: the tranche sits at the 84.7th Calmar percentile in-sample and the fixed Wednesday/Thursday books at about 85. Under the regular-spacing 13-week-block null, Friday's H2 Calmar percentile is 94.5-95.7 across 6 seeds, so the key table's 'robust' label for H2 is not supported. The verdict is unaffected because B fails.

Criterion B was close to predetermined. Round 1 already showed Friday ranked 5 / 3 / 4 on SPX / RUT / TSX with identical F2 machinery, so B needed 5 of the remaining 5 markets. The 'before any round-2 number' timing cannot be verified.

Planning numbers are mislabelled. The '-29.5% single fixed day median maxDD' is the 13-week-block null; the 5 actual fixed-day F2 books have a median of -28.3% (CAGR median 16.87%). Tranche figures move by about 0.3pp CAGR, 0.9pp maxDD and 0.03 Calmar depending on whether daily returns or sub-account equity curves are averaged.

Framing is overstated in C4 (median year +3.06pp exceeds the mean; 29/39 years positive), C5 (no-change weeks carry 32% of the H2 gap) and C9 (Monday is the worst book in only 4/8 markets in H1 and 3/8 in H2).
C11 states the E4 range as 77-99%, but 1988 is 34%. The IXIC Wednesday statistic is not produced by the script or JSON; I verified it is true (+22.4bp, t 6.43).

About 1pp of the 4.66pp OOS Friday advantage comes from the Aug x0.5 seasonal-boundary quirk. Friday's 2026-07-31 decision fell in July, so full size was held through 08-07; the gap is 3.65pp with the seasonal rule off.

verifications.lens: ROBUSTNESS (overfitting, period-boundary and single-episode sensitivity, null/placebo design, bootstrap, multiple testing, cross-market fragility, economic plausibility)
verifications.rule_applied_correctly: Yes, as written. I re-ran r2_friday_effect.py with its output sent to a scratch file, and every numeric leaf matches the saved JSON (0 differences). An independent rebuild with common.backtest and common.stats gives the same F2 gaps: H1 +2.925pp CAGR / +0.1917 Calmar, H2 +1.951pp / +0.1746. A rebuilt per-week placebo (seed 20261118) puts Friday's Calmar at the 99.3rd percentile in H1 and 99.6th in H2. So A = true. The cross-market rebuild gives B = 3/7 (5 needed), so the result is 'not structural' and the planning basis is the tranche. Diagnostic (b) for F2 also matches as written: lag 2 removes 52.7% of the gap and the first-day share is 24.1%, so it is false. Two limits: (1) I cannot verify the claim that the rule was fixed before any round-2 number existed, because the docstring has an 'ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN' section and there is no version history. (2) The verdict holds in direction, but the rule is fragile in places. Under the both-metric B test, 0 of 48 alternative constructions reach 5/7. A single-metric reading of B would pass: Calmar-only gives 5/7 at the spec construction, and CAGR-only with holiday substitution gives 5/7. A itself would fail without 2022, at 5 of 7 EMA spans, and under some regular-spacing nulls. A failing would only strengthen 'not structural'.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly: A holds (H1 +2.925pp/+0.1917, H2 +1.951pp/+0.1746, placebo 99.3/99.6). B = 3/7: SPX -0.718/-0.0979, RUT +0.325/+0.0001, TSX -0.556/+0.0076, HSI -0.200/-0.0228, DAX -0.120/+0.0047, N225 +1.466/+0.0448, IXIC +1.687/+0.0920. The 'not structural' direction is robust. Under the pre-registered both-metric test, 0 of 48 alternative constructions reach 5/7 (range 2-4). The 48 are: HSI panel or own calendar, TSX panel or own calendar (^GSPTSE), 6 window choices (spec, first+500 sessions, all from 1990, common 1988-12-28, N225/IXIC from 1988, all from 1993), and skip or substitute holidays. Sharpe-only and a material-margin version (>0.25pp and >0.02) never exceed 3/7. Fragility: Calmar-only B gives 5/7 at the spec construction (11 of 48 constructions reach 5 or more), because the passes in RUT/TSX/DAX are only +0.0001/+0.0076/+0.0047. CAGR-only with holiday substitution gives 5-6/7 (20 of 48). A fails if 2022 is removed (H2 Calmar gap +0.041, placebo percentile 93.9).
verdicts.corrected: B under the spec metric across 48 constructions: 2-4/7 (never 5). Calmar-only reading: 5/7 at the spec construction.

verdicts.reason: An independent common.backtest rebuild matches. F1: 11.876/-19.20/0.619 vs 10.901/-20.79/0.524. F2: 19.715/-23.96/0.823 vs 17.289/-27.68/0.625. F3: 24.134/-29.99/0.805 vs 20.885/-32.50/0.643. F2 decade CAGR gaps are +4.08/+2.79/+2.04/+2.83/+1.35. The CAGR gap is positive in all 15 tier x decade cells (smallest: F1 2020s +0.39pp, F3 2020s +0.71pp). The Calmar gap is positive in 14 of 15 cells; F1 in the 2000s is -0.023.
verdicts.corrected: Positive in every tier and decade on CAGR; on Calmar 14/15 (F1 2000s -0.023).

verdicts.reason: The rebuilt per-week placebo is identical: IS 100.0/99.9, H1 98.0/99.3, H2 99.1/99.6, and 0 of 1,000 schedules beat Friday in both halves. The in-sample extremeness survives every stress I tried: two more per-week seeds (99.9/99.9); block nulls of 4, 13 (4 seeds), 26 and 52 weeks (IS Calmar 99.0-99.9); and a selection-adjusted null where each random schedule picks its best EMA from the July grid {100,125,150,200,250}. In that null Friday's 0.823 is still at the 99.9th percentile (null median 0.605, 95th percentile 0.741). A paired block bootstrap gives IS p(gap<=0) <= 0.003 for blocks of 21, 63 and 252 days. The half-level evidence is weaker than the per-week numbers suggest. Under regular-spacing nulls, H2 Calmar sits at 95.6/95.3/95.9/94.8 (block-13, four seeds), 96.2 (block-4), 95.3 (block-26) and 93.9 (block-52). verdicts.corrected: H2 Friday Calmar percentile under regular-spacing nulls: 93.9-96.2, not 99.6.

verdicts.reason: All figures reproduce: 2.112pp/yr; 1,374 of 9,712 disagreement days carry 80.2%; Friday-in/other-out days carry 74.3%; 216 episodes, 135 positive; top 10 = 49.1%, top 20 = 78.6%; Friday ahead in 29/39 years (13/19, 16/20); 1998 Friday +118.7% vs tranche +87.4%; top 5 years = 59.3% of the log gap; mean 2.81 falls to 1.57 without the top 3 years. Removing any single episode tested (1988-89, 1989-90, 1998, 2000-02, GFC, 2012, 2018, COVID, 2025 tariff) keeps the IS gap between +1.92 and +2.57pp and A intact. 2022 is the only exception: it breaks A through the H2 Calmar.

The numbers reproduce: switch +0.90 (43%), near-EMA +0.46, size-only +1.14 (54%), no-change +0.07 (3%), QLD +2.22 / IEF -0.11 / costs +0.007, 189 vs 214-217 switches. But 'no-change weeks carry almost none' is an in-sample cancellation. In H1 they contribute -0.40pp/yr; in H2 they contribute +0.54pp/yr, 32% of the H2 gap, about the same as switch weeks (+0.56) and size-only weeks (+0.61). Friday's 189 switches are unusual: 0.55th percentile of the block-13 null (median 209.5, minimum 187) and 1.75th of the per-week null. Friday has the fewest switches in both halves (H1 99 vs 106-119; H2 90 vs 98-110). Across block-13 schedules, the switch count correlates -0.42 with CAGR.
verdicts.corrected: H2 gap splits into roughly equal thirds: switch 0.56 / size-only 0.61 / no-change 0.54 pp/yr.

verdicts.reason: The overall diagnostic is computed as pre-registered: lag 2 removes 52.7% of the gap and the first-day share is 24.1%, so it is false. The H2 part also holds: the lag-2 gap is +2.34 vs +1.95, and Monday's share is -16%. But 'explains the H1 part completely' fails the pre-registered criterion (ii) when applied to H1. The H1 first-day share is 52.2% (F1 48.2%, F3 56.9%), below the 66.7% needed. Only the lag-2 leg passes (103% for F2; F1 H1 +1.16 to -0.19; F3 +4.08 to -0.07).
verdicts.corrected: H1: lag 2 removes 103%, but only 52% of the arithmetic gap is earned on the first session, so the two-part test is not met in H1 either.

verdicts.reason: The numbers reproduce. NDX Friday-to-next-session 1988-99: Pearson +0.255, Spearman +0.296 (+0.264 with the 10 largest Friday moves trimmed), vs -0.19 to +0.05 for the other weekdays. Later: 2000-06 +0.008, 2007-26 +0.003. SPX 1988-99 +0.067; IXIC 1975-87 +0.497. NDX day-to-day autocorrelation 1985-89 +0.179; NDX leads IXIC by a day (+0.325). Mondays after Friday switch-offs average -70.9bp in H1 (n=49) vs +1.4bp in H2 (n=45). H1 Friday premiums vanish at lag 2 in HSI (-1.15), DAX (-1.57), N225 (-0.50) and IXIC (+0.06). The 'stale Nasdaq closes' explanation is not supported. Friday has the highest next-session Spearman of the five weekdays in all 7 other markets in-sample, including SPX, DAX, N225, HSI and TSX, and in 5 of 7 in their H2. Monday has the lowest in 7 of 7. Stale closes in general cannot explain this: NDX day-to-day autocorrelation in 1990-99 is only +0.02, while Friday-to-Monday is +0.23 in 1994-99. 'Expired' holds for P&L (the Monday share of the H2 gap is -16%). On NDX, however, Friday is still the least-reverting weekday after 2007: Pearson 2007-16 +0.09 vs -0.29 to -0.05, and 2017-26 -0.08 vs -0.26 to -0.10.
verdicts.corrected: The Friday-to-Monday continuation is a cross-market weekend pattern (Friday highest in 7/7 markets in-sample), not specific to Nasdaq closes. Its P&L effect has expired; Friday's relative ranking has not.

verdicts.reason: The mean/timing split reproduces: -0.033 vs +2.138pp/yr (H1 -0.004 / +2.515; H2 -0.062 / +1.774). Friday's exposure minus the 5-book average on each return weekday is within ±0.0023. NDX Monday mean is -0.3/-8.7/+10.8bp by era; Monday minus the rest is -13.7bp (t -1.99, variance 1.43x), -10.4bp (t -0.91), +4.2bp (t +0.80). This holds only for the mean channel. The in-sample figures reproduce. Monday is the worst Calmar book in 6/7 markets; its placebo percentiles are 1.3-14.6; it ranks last in 45/45 grid configurations. On NDX, Monday stays last after removing 1998, 2000-02, the GFC, COVID or 2022, and after holiday substitution (14.11% / -36.1%). But the pattern does not hold within halves. Monday is the worst Calmar book in only 3/7 markets in H1 and 3/7 in H2. With holiday substitution it is 5/7 in-sample and 2/7 in each half. A plausible mechanism exists ('turnaround Tuesday'): Monday has the lowest next-session Spearman in 7/7 markets in-sample and 5/7 in H2. Under the B metric, Monday beats the tranche in 0/7 markets.
verdicts.corrected: Monday worst Calmar: 6/7 in-sample, 3/7 in H1, 3/7 in H2 (holiday substitution: 5/7, 2/7, 2/7).

verdicts.reason: The span grid reproduces exactly. CAGR gap: +1.14/+2.17/+2.43/+1.16/+0.87/+0.36/-0.02. Calmar gap: -0.002/+0.178/+0.198/+0.002/+0.003/+0.082/+0.079. H2 median +0.455. The research log confirms the July grid was SMA/EMA 100-250 on weekly (Friday) rebalancing. The full criterion A holds at only 2 of 7 spans (75 and 100); within the July grid, only at 100. At span 50, Friday's H1 placebo percentile is 60.4; at 125 and 150 the H2 Calmar gap is negative. But tuning alone does not explain the in-sample outlier: the selection-adjusted null still puts Friday at the 99.9th percentile (C3).

The NDX calendar matches ^GSPC (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 weekend rows). There are 2 zero-return days in 1985-90 (one Monday, one Wednesday). Same-day correlation with IXIC is 0.94-0.99, and the largest one-day lead or lag is 0.325. mark matches the W-FRI rule. Holiday substitution leaves the gap at +2.419 vs +2.426. Holiday weeks: Friday 68, Monday 183. Options-expiry Fridays carry 39.4% of the gap on 455 of 1,944 weeks (t 1.12). The 1985-99 Wednesday mean is +32.4bp (t 6.55) on NDX, +22.4bp (t 6.43) on IXIC and +12.0bp (t 3.80) on SPX. NDX-IXIC Wednesday correlation is 0.94, the same as other days, so it is not an NDX data error. One detail is wrong: in 1988 only 34.4% of NDX opens equal the prior close.
