verdicts.reason: The F2 block-13 numbers reproduce and are stable across 4 seeds: CAGR mean 17.14-17.19%, maxDD median -29.2% to -29.5%, 5th percentile -34.4%. Block-26 and block-52 nulls give maxDD medians of -29.7% and -28.7%. The F3 figure of -37.1% comes from the per-week null, which the specialist itself calls pessimistic. Under the block-13 null used for F2, F3's single-day median maxDD is -35.6% (5th percentile -39.4%), with CAGR median 20.6% and Calmar 0.58. F1 under block-13: 10.87% / -20.6% (5th percentile -23.0%) / 0.53. Note that most books' in-sample maxDD, the tranche's included, falls in the same 2021-11 to 2022 episode.
verdicts.corrected: F3 single-day median maxDD -35.6% (block-13 null; 5th percentile -39.4%), not -37.1%.

verdicts.reason: OOS reproduces: F2 Friday -6.03% vs tranche -10.69% (Mon -9.38, Tue -13.19, Wed -12.90, Thu -12.22), 90.5th percentile (placebo median -11.78%). F3 -8.99 vs -14.91 (92.4th); F1 -4.41 vs -6.61 (90.7th). The 20 OOS days with a gap of at least 30bp fall in two windows. Jul 29 - Aug 7 adds about +3.66pp: Friday was in at 0.425 from its Jul 24 decision while the Mon/Tue/Wed books were out. Oct 2 - Nov 5 adds about +2.43pp net: Friday was out from its Oct 16 decision. Together that is 6.09pp of the 5.14pp summed daily gap. That is two events, as stated.

issues: Single-episode dependence (2022). Friday's in-sample and H2 maxDD advantage (-24.0% vs tranche -27.7%) comes entirely from the 2021-11-19 to 2022 drawdown. With 2022 returns set to zero for every book and placebo, the H2 Calmar gap drops from +0.175 to +0.041, the H2 placebo percentile falls to 93.9, and criterion A fails. If Friday had the tranche's maxDD, the H2 percentile would be 91.7. Removing any other episode tested (1988-89, 1989-90, 1998, 2000-02, GFC, 2012, 2018, COVID, 2025) keeps A intact.

The null used by criterion A flatters Friday. The per-week null spaces rebalances irregularly, which pulls its mean CAGR down to 16.52-16.54% (vs 17.05-17.19% for block nulls) and puts the tranche at the 77th-79th CAGR percentile. Under regular-spacing nulls, Friday's H2 Calmar percentile is 95.6/95.3/95.9/94.8 (block-13, four seeds), 96.2 (block-4), 95.3 (block-26) and 93.9 (block-52). Two of these 7 regular-spacing runs fall below 95. The rule as written uses the per-week null, so A still passes.

A holds at only 2 of 7 EMA spans (75 and 100), and only at 100 within the July 100-250 grid. Changing the half split: A passes for every split from 2000 to 2016, but fails for 1994, 1996 and 1998 (H1 placebo 92.5-93.4).

B fails robustly under the pre-registered both-metric rule: 0 of 48 alternative constructions reach 5/7 (range 2-4). The specialist's caveat that the result holds 'under every reading tried' leaves out one reading that flips it. Calmar-only gives 5/7 at the spec construction (RUT +0.0001, TSX +0.0076, DAX +0.0047 count as passes), and 11 of 48 constructions reach 5 or more. CAGR-only with holiday substitution gives 5-6/7 (20 of 48). Sharpe-only (at most 3/7) and a material-margin test (at most 3/7) agree with the rule.

The knife-edge markets flip with immaterial conventions. RUT passes at only 2 of 8 start years (1988-09-07 and 1991). Holiday substitution turns RUT, HSI and DAX CAGR gaps positive and their Calmar gaps negative, and does the reverse for TSX. HSI's fail is a construction artifact: on its own calendar it passes at all 8 start years (+0.25 to +0.63pp, +0.019 to +0.033). TSX on its own calendar fails on both metrics (-0.165 / -0.0035).

Friday's 3/7 under B is ordinary. Scoring every weekday the same way gives Mon 0, Tue 3, Wed 1, Thu 4, Fri 3. On CAGR alone: Mon 1, Tue 6, Wed 5, Thu 6, Fri 3. A persistently weak Monday book drags the tranche down, which makes 'beats the tranche' an easy bar to clear. At lag 2, Friday's B count drops to 2/7.

Paired circular block bootstrap of Friday minus tranche CAGR: in-sample p <= 0.003 and H1 p = 0.007-0.012 for blocks of 21, 63 and 252 days. In H2, p = 0.036-0.055, with lower 95% bounds of -0.19 to -0.44pp. The H2 premium on its own is borderline-significant.

The NDX premium mechanically tracks unusually few whipsaws. Friday's 189 in-sample switches sit at the 0.55th percentile of the block-13 null, and Friday has the fewest switches in both halves. Across schedules, switch count correlates -0.42 with CAGR. In other markets Friday has the fewest switches in only 3 of 7 (RUT, HSI, IXIC).

Selection-adjusted null (my addition): even when each random schedule picks its best EMA from {100,125,150,200,250}, Friday's 0.823 in-sample Calmar is at the 99.9th percentile (null 95th percentile 0.741). Tuning EMA-100 does not explain the in-sample NDX outlier. The decision still rests on the failed cross-market replication.

Mechanism attribution: the cross-market weekday pattern (Friday has the highest next-session Spearman in 7/7 markets in-sample and 5/7 in H2; Monday the lowest in 7/7) contradicts 'stale Nasdaq closes' (C7). It also qualifies the recommendation's 'appears only on NDX'. In H2, Friday beats the tranche on both metrics in RUT, N225 and IXIC, and N225 Friday ranks first by Calmar in-sample, in H1 and in H2.

dims.title: Scenario stress of today's book and re-entry behaviour
dims.task: SCENARIO STRESS (descriptive only - no parameter selection). Current state at the 2026-11-17 close: NDX 27,002, EMA-100 28,968, vol20 35.5%, er20 0.26, 10y 5.10%; F1/F2/F3-IEF are risk-off holding 85% IEF + 15% GLD. Build a forward simulator that appends a scenario path of daily NDX returns (plus IEF and gold returns) to the panel history and re-computes EMA-100/vol20/er20 and the weekly decisions exactly as the rules do (Friday book; also report the tranche). Scenarios: (S1) 10y yield +100bp / -100bp over 1 month, equities flat (IEF via duration 7.09 and convexity 77); (S2) gold -15% / +15% over 2 months; (S3) V-rebound: NDX climbs back to the 2026-10-06 record (31,224) over 6 weeks then +1%/month for 6 months, yields -25bp; (S4) 2022-like continuation: NDX -25% over 6 months with the 10y +75bp and gold -10%; (S5) deflationary bust: NDX -35% over 9 months with the 10y -150bp and gold +10%; (S6) whipsaw: NDX oscillates about +/-8% around its EMA for 6 months. Use realistic daily noise (e.g. daily vol consistent with 25-35% annualised, deterministic seed) and report results for several seeds. Also HISTORICAL PATH REPLAYS: take the actual daily return paths of NDX, IEF (spliced) and gold_phys starting at 2018-12-07, 2022-01-21, 2000-04-14, 2011-08-05, 2025-04-04, 2020-03-06, 2015-08-24, 1990-08-10, 1998-08-31 and apply them forward from today's state. For every scenario report: 1/3/6/12-month returns of F1/F2/F3, QQQ and QLD buy-and-hold, max drawdown, the re-entry date and the NDX level at re-entry, the number of whipsaws, and the share of the rebound captured. Summarise what the strategy is and is not protected against from today's position.

result.headline: Stress test of today's book, which is fully risk-off: on 2026-11-17 (an out-of-sample state) all 15 books, F1/F2/F3 x Mon-Fri, hold 85% IEF + 15% GLD. The strategy protects against equity bear markets. Over 12 months F2 makes -9.6% to -12.7% in rates-up and AI-bust bears and +3.7% in a deflationary bust, against QQQ -20% to -54% and QLD -45% to -86%; F2 maxDD stays between -15% and -19%. It does not protect against three things. First, its own off-leg: the 10y +100bp costs about -5.5pp within a month, and gold -15% costs -1.25 to -2.25pp. Second, re-entry lag in a V-rebound: the median re-entry is 2026-12-11 near NDX 29,650, +9.8% above today, and only about half of the rebound is earned. Third, range-bound high-volatility markets: F2 makes -7.4% in a flat 30%-vol year and -33% to -38% under a +/-8% oscillation around the EMA. That is worse than QLD buy-and-hold and beyond the in-sample worst 12 months (-21%). F1 is the most robust tier in every adverse scenario.
decisions: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No strategy parameter is chosen or ranked. The July rules run unchanged through common.strategy_weights and common.backtest (lag 1, 3 bp, IEF off-leg, 15% gold_phys). Tiers: F1 QQQ vt 0.20, F2 QLD vt 0.30, F3 TQQQ vt 0.20. Books: the Friday book plus the 5-weekday tranche, using the main_tranche_check.py convention. No decision rule was pre-registered for this dimension, so none was applied.

Forward simulator: 252 NYSE trading days from 2026-11-18 are appended to the panel history. ema100 (recursion from the panel's last value, which equals ewm(span=100, adjust=False)), above, vol20, er20 and month are recomputed exactly as panel.py does. Holiday Fridays 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01, 2027-03-26 and 2027-06-18 get no Friday mark, as with P.mark.

Sleeves come from the path: qqq = ndx - 0.20%/252; qld = 2*ndx - 0.95%/252 - rf_d; tqqq = 3*ndx - 0.95%/252 - 2*rf_d. rf is held at the 11-17 value of 4.138% for every scenario and replay, i.e. today's cost of leverage.

Synthetic IEF is a price function of the cumulative 10y change: f(dy) = 1 - 7.09*dy + 0.5*76.9*dy^2, plus carry (y_{t-1} + 0.305% panel alpha)/252. This captures the convexity of the whole move. TLT (15.8 / 134.4, parallel 30y shift) and a 50/50 IEF/BIL off-leg appear only as reference static books.

Noise: Brownian bridges that hit each scenario skeleton exactly at its pins. NDX vol is 30% (sensitivities 25% and 35%). The 10y uses 4.0 bp/day and gold 28.1%/yr, both trailing-252-day realised to the freeze; post-freeze values are 4.4 bp and 28.8%. Noise is Gaussian and independent across series. Seeds are shared by every scenario (common random numbers): 40 at 30%, 20 at each other setting.

Disclosed change after the first run: the primary noise was switched from monthly pins (design B) to pins only at the scenario's own waypoints plus day 252 (design A). B forces month-end mean reversion (VR21 0.35, VR63 0.11 vs NDX 0.81/0.85) and produced 7.6 whipsaws/yr in flat markets, against a historical maximum of 6. B is kept and reported as a range-bound stress.

Disclosed add-ons after the first results, all counted: an S0 all-flat control, which shares every seed's NDX path with S1/S2 so S1/S2 minus S0 isolates the pure rate or gold shock; S3c, the same V with post-climb noise vol set to the in-sample median vol20 of 18.5%, because real V-recoveries calm down; and a 5%-noise diagnostic run that separates skeleton effects from whipsaw effects.

After each scenario's stated window the skeleton stays flat at its end level while noise continues. S6 uses c = today's EMA (28,968) with the phase set so the path starts at today's level and rises. Periods are T = 42 days (S6a) and 21 days (S6b), run for 126 days.

Historical replays apply the actual NDX, spliced IEF and gold_phys daily returns from today's state. The primary 'literal' convention makes day 1 the return dated X. result.recommendation:
This stress test supports no rule or parameter change. It is descriptive and selects nothing. Write the following down now, before the Nov 25 PCE, the Dec 8-9 FOMC and the Dec 10 CPI.

(1) WHAT YOU ARE EXPOSED TO TODAY IS THE OFF-LEG, NOT THE NASDAQ.
- A 10y move of +100bp costs about -5.5% of the whole account within a month.
- Gold -15% costs another -1.25% to -2.25%.
- Together that is about -8%.
- A rally in yields (-100bp) adds about +6.4%.
- If the +100bp case is unacceptable, the lever is the open off-leg decision, not the equity timing:
  - Static IEF.
  - The parameter-free 50/50 IEF/BIL, which halves the shock to -2.85%. The critic found it costs about 1pp/yr and fails 1988-2006.
- Confirm the live account holds IEF and not TLT. TLT more than doubles the shock to -12.9%.

(2) RE-ENTRY PLAN.
- On Friday 2026-11-20 the book re-enters only if NDX closes above about 28,891 (+7.0%).
- If NDX stays flat, the bar drifts down: about 28,430 by 12-11 and about 28,000 by 01-08 (no marks on 12-25 or 01-01).
- The first re-entry at today's vol would be about 72% QLD for F2, or 48% TQQQ for F3. Both are 1.44x NDX, and both are halved if er20 < 0.25.
- In a V-shaped recovery, expect re-entry around mid-December near NDX 29,000-30,000. That means missing roughly a third to two-thirds of a sharp climb and earning about half of the rebound.
- If the rebound keeps trending, F2 roughly keeps pace with QQQ (2020, 2025 replays). If it stalls into a choppy grind, F2 can trail QQQ by 15-25pp (2018 replay, S3).

(3) EXPECTATIONS TO SET.
- Bears are where the rules pay: F2 -10% to -13% against QQQ -20% to -54% and QLD -45% to -86%. F2 maxDD stays near -15% to -19%.
- Flat or range-bound high-volatility markets are where they lose:
  - About -7% for F2 in a trendless 30%-vol year.
  - About -33% to -38% in a violent +/-8% range around the EMA.
  - That is worse than simply holding QLD.
- 3 or more whipsaws in a year is normal in such markets. On its own it does not show the rules are broken.
- A 12-month F2 loss beyond about -21% would be outside the in-sample record. Treat it as a monitoring flag, alongside the critic's pre-committed -35% maxDD review trigger.

(4) TIER CHOICE UNDER STRESS.
- F1 is the most robust in every adverse scenario.
- At today's vol, F2 and F3 carry identical NDX exposure and stress almost identically.
- F3's extra return appears only in strong trends.

(5) Judge live results against the 5-weekday tranche. In replays, a single Friday book's 12-month result swings by about 4pp on average, and up to 16pp, from weekday phase alone.
caveats: Synthetic noise is Gaussian and independent across NDX, 10y and gold, at constant vol (except S3c). There is no volatility clustering, no fat tails and no stock-bond correlation regime; the recent 63-day corr(NDX, d10y) is +0.20. Real stress usually raises vol, which shrinks re-entry size through the vol target.
Skeletons stay flat after each scenario's stated window. That assumption shapes the 12-month figures for S1, S2, S4, S5 and S6.

S6 is a designed worst case for trend following. S6b's swings of about 16% every 10 trading days are more violent than almost any historical period. S3's +1%/month grind is a weak trend relative to 30% noise.

Design choices were changed after seeing results: the primary noise moved from B to A, and S0, S3c and a 5%-noise diagnostic were added. All are disclosed and counted in the 84 variants. None selects or tunes a strategy parameter. The calm vol in S3c is an objective in-sample statistic (median vol20 18.5%).

Replays map historical days onto forward weekdays arbitrarily, so Friday-book replay results carry large phase luck: mean absolute Friday-minus-tranche gap 4.3pp. The in-sample Friday premium does not show up in replays (mean +0.5pp). That is expected and is not a test of the Friday effect.

Replay data limits:
- Pre-2002-07-30 IEF is synthetic (calibrated).
- Gold before 2000-08-30 is a monthly-average interpolation that understates daily vol. This affects the 1990, 1998 and part of the 2000 replays.
- LETF financing uses today's 4.14% bill rate, while NDX and IEF returns embed their own era's rates. Re-basing IEF carry to today's 5.10% changes F2 12m by -2.5 to +2.3pp.

The replay convention matters for single paths. Literal (day 1 = return on X) vs 'after' (day 1 = X+1) moves F2 12m by up to 26pp, in the 2020 case (+44.9% vs +18.4%). Both conventions are stored in the JSON.

Forward sleeves are simulated (2x/3x NDX minus 0.95% minus financing). Round 1 found real TQQQ trailed its sim by about 0.6pp/yr at today's rates, so the forward 2x/3x numbers may be slightly optimistic.

Scenario outcomes are conditional illustrations, not probabilities or forecasts. Medians come from 40 seeds, with p10/p90 bands in the JSON. Differences under about 2pp between unpaired scenarios are within seed noise.
The starting state (2026-11-17) is out-of-sample context. Noise calibration and all replay paths use data to the 2026-07-24 freeze only.

verdicts.reason: The criticism of design B stands. Three problems remain. (a) The NDX figures (0.81/0.85) were not computed with the same 252-day estimator; they are full-sample. With the windowed estimator, NDX gives VR21 0.73 and VR63 0.51, between design A (0.95/0.74) and design B (0.35/0.11). (b) The estimator de-means each window, so 'identical to an unpinned random walk' is guaranteed by construction. With a known-mean estimator, the design-A bridge has VR 0.91 / 0.74 / 0.50 at 21 / 63 / 126 days, against 0.99 for a random walk. The day-252 pin removes the convexity of trend following. Dropping it moves the F2 median in S0 from -5.7% to -2.4% (mean from -3.3% to +3.0%), in S3 from -3.1% to +2.0%, and in S4 from -9.4% to -6.3%. (c) The extra choppiness comes from zero drift, not from the noise structure. Block-bootstrapped real NDX returns give the same S0 whipsaw rate (3.68 vs 3.71 a year), and so does 5% noise (3.3 a year).
verdicts.corrected: Design A is random-walk-like at short horizons only. The day-252 pin adds mean reversion that lowers F2 medians by 3-5pp compared with unpinned noise. NDX is more mean-reverting than design A when measured with the same windowed estimator.

issues: Seed noise: 40 seeds leave about 2.5-3pp of standard error on the F2 12-month medians. At 500 seeds: S0 -7.4% becomes -5.7%; S1+ -12.4% becomes -9.9%; S2- -9.6% becomes -7.9%; S3 F2 -1.2% becomes -3.1%; S3 tranche +2.1% becomes -3.1%; S5 +3.7% becomes +6.2%. The specialist's S3 and S5 batches sit at the extremes of twelve 40-seed batches (S3 is at the top of -7.6..-1.2; S5 at the bottom of +3.7..+10.0).

Design A pins every path at day 252 (disclosed, but its effect is not measured). Every path ends exactly on its skeleton, which removes the dispersion of 12-month NDX returns and the convexity of trend following. Without the pin, F2 medians rise 3-5pp: S0 -2.4%, S3 +2.0%, S4 -6.3%, S5 +8.3%, and the S0 mean turns positive (+3.0%). The variance-ratio evidence offered for design A's realism cannot detect the pin.

Replays are single paths that depend on weekday phase. The literal convention starts each path on the replay date's own down day (NDX -4.3% on average), which the risk-off book avoids and QQQ absorbs. Shifting the start by up to ±10 days moves F2 Friday 12-month results by up to ±20pp: 2022 -23.9% to +1.5%, 2020 +18.4% to +57.4%. The count of replays where F2 beats QQQ is 2-6 of 9 across start offsets within ±5 days.

Drawdown in bears is understated. From today's state, the 2022 path gives F2 Friday a median maxDD of -20.6% and a worst of -33.0% across ±10 start offsets, close to the critic's -35% review trigger. Two of 21 paths lose more than the in-sample worst 12 months (-21.3%), so the proposed -21% flag can trip in a plain 2022 repeat. The headline 'F2 maxDD stays between -15% and -19%' rests on one alignment of weekdays. If live results are judged on the tranche, as recommendation (5) says, the in-sample worst to compare against is -25.3%, not -21%.

Re-entry size is overstated for the near term. A re-entry on 11-20 or 11-27 would come with er20 at about 0.00-0.05, because NDX would be back at its level of 20 trading days earlier (10-23 close 28,958; 10-30 close 28,385). The chop rule would halve the position, and vol20 would be 37-44%. That makes F2/F3 about 0.6-0.7x NDX, not 1.44x.

The off-leg risk is framed too narrowly around rates. On trailing-year vols the Euler risk shares are about 50/50 between IEF and gold (77/23 on long-run vols). S1 is a 5.4-sigma move that has not happened since 1988 (largest 21-day rise +95bp). Recommendation (1)'s rates-centred framing understates the gold leg, which is half of today's risk.

S6 depends on construction. Its severity comes from quarter-cycle pins that force the oscillation. Its whipsaw rate (5-6 per 6 months) exceeds the in-sample maximum of 4 in any 6-month window. With unpinned noise, F2 is no worse than QLD buy-and-hold (-12.5% / -19.4%). Cycles of 63 days or longer cost only about 9%. The S6 loss is robust only for cycles of 9-42 days that are enforced by pins.

The trendless-year loss is a property of the model. In-sample, risk-off starts followed by a flat high-vol year (NDX within ±10%, realised vol at least 25%; 77 days in 7 episodes) gave F2 a median 12-month return of +18.7%, with only 6% of starts negative. The 9-13pp cost of bear-rally re-entries falls to 3.5-7.7pp with unpinned or block-bootstrap noise.

Minor: the bar falls at most 0.135% a day and less than 0.1% a day after mid-December, not 0.1-0.2%. 'All five books by day 21' is a median of day 22 (lower-median date 2026-12-18). In C2, attributing persistence to the 58% risk-off share is a non-sequitur. In C10, the NDX variance ratios are labelled as using the same 252-day estimator but are full-sample.

dims.title: Sensitivity to model-input corrections
dims.task: MODEL-INPUT SENSITIVITY. (a) FINANCING SPREAD: the pre-inception leveraged sims borrow at the T-bill rate. Calibrate a financing spread (and/or expense gap) on real QLD (2006-06+) and real TQQQ (2010-02+) vs their sims, by rate regime (e.g. regress the daily real-minus-sim difference on rf_d and a constant; check stability across 2010-15, 2016-21, 2022-26). Apply the calibrated spread to the pre-inception sims and rerun F1/F2/F3-IEF on the Friday book and the tranche. (b) DURATION: replace the fixed calibrated duration of the pre-2002 synthetic IEF/TLT with the analytic modified duration and convexity of a par bond (7.5y for IEF, 20y for TLT) at the prevailing yield; check fit vs the real ETFs 2002+ (it must not be worse than the fixed calibration by more than a little); rerun. (c) PRE-2000 GOLD: replace the log-interpolated monthly-average series with (i) month-end step returns (the whole monthly return booked on the month's last trading day) and (ii) gold_miners; rerun. Report deltas in CAGR / maxDD / Calmar for each tier on both bases, separately and combined, and state whether ANY round-1 conclusion changes (2x vs 3x, IEF vs bills, gold vs IEF, chop/vol value, edge vs QQQ).

result.headline: The three model-input corrections together cost F3 about 0.7pp/yr of in-sample CAGR and F2 about 0.3pp/yr. Almost all of it comes from financing costs in the pre-2010 leveraged sims. Calmar changes by -0.017 (F3) and -0.014 (F2) on Fridays, and -0.008 / -0.013 on the tranche. Applying the pre-registered rules, none of the 48 round-1 status items flips on the Friday basis under any correction. On the tranche basis, 2 of 48 flip, and both are knife-edge. (1) F2's Calmar edge over QQQ loses 95% significance: the lower bound moves from +0.011 to -0.002 while P(edge > 0) only moves from 0.979 to 0.974, and the flip does not hold across bootstrap seeds. (2) F2's 1988-2006 IEF-over-TLT Calmar edge goes from +0.076 to -0.007 (combination with miners only). The 2x vs 3x, IEF vs bills, gold vs IEF, chop/vol and F3-vs-QQQ conclusions are unchanged. Out-of-sample results are identical by construction.
decisions: Primary financing calibration uses a dividend-neutral gap: real ETF minus [lev*(QQQ_real + 0.20%/yr) - 0.95%/yr - (lev-1)*rf]. The panel sims use the NDX PRICE return, so in the literal regression (real - sim on [1, rf_d]) the intercept and slope absorb the NDX dividend yield. The literal intercept exceeds the dividend-neutral one by 1.89%/yr (QLD) and 3.18%/yr (TQQQ), about lev x 1%. The literal fit was still run and applied as a sensitivity (A_lit).

Each fund's own pooled fit (alpha + beta*rf_d, data to 2026-07-24) was applied only on days without a real ETF (QLD before 2006-06-22, TQQQ before 2010-02-12). F1 holds unlevered QQQ, so (a) cannot change it.
Stress bound A_stress: a constant drag equal to the worst regime mean dividend-neutral gap per unit borrowed (QLD 2006-09, 2.15%/yr), i.e. QLD -2.15%/yr and TQQQ -4.31%/yr.

Duration fit gate set in advance: TE <= 1.10x fixed, corr >= fixed - 0.01, |CAGR gap| <= |fixed gap| + 0.25pp, on 2002-07-31..2026-07-24. The pure analytic par bond (B) passed for IEF and TLT and is used in the combinations. The level-matched version B_k (k*D_par) is reported as a sensitivity.

Gold C1 books each month's interpolated gross return on its last trading day, keeping the cumulative return exactly (-15.0% over 1985-10..2000-08-30) and the 0.40%/yr fee. C2 substitutes ^XAU miners on the same days.
Combinations: ALL1 = A_div + B + C1 (primary); ALL2 = A_div + B + C2.

Round-1 conclusions were encoded as 48 status items per basis (R1 2x/3x, R2 IEF/bills, R3 gold/IEF, R4 chop and vol target, R5 vs QQQ, R6 IEF/TLT). A change = status differs from the uncorrected panel run by the same code on the same basis (IS 1988-01-01..2026-07-24). Bootstrap: 63-day blocks, 2000 draws, seed 0, the round-1 scheme.
For runtime, the bootstrap was restricted to the 7 series the rules use (F1-F3 default, F1-F3 gold-in-IEF, QQQ). This was decided after a 50-draw smoke test and does not change any rule input.
Added after seeing the flips, information only: a 5-seed re-draw of the flipped bootstrap item. It does not alter the rule's verdict.
Applied the rule as written. The flips count as formal changes even though they are within bootstrap noise.

claims.claim: The literal real-minus-sim regression the brief suggests measures dividends as well as financing, because the panel sims are price-only. The dividend-neutral gap isolates financing, expense and friction costs: about 0.7-1.4%/yr per unit borrowed, rising with the rate regime.
claims.evidence: Pooled to 2026-07-24, Newey-West SEs. Literal: QLD alpha +0.84%/yr (se 0.34), beta -0.175 (0.109); TQQQ +1.27% (0.51), beta -0.369 (0.146). Literal regime means: QLD +1.62 / +1.04 / +0.27 and TQQQ +2.11 / +0.48 / -0.73 (2010-15 / 2016-21 / 2022-frz). Dividend-neutral: QLD alpha -1.05% (0.27), beta -0.03 (0.09); TQQQ -1.91% (0.46), beta -0.18 (0.13). 1. Keep every round-1 decision. 2x (F2) stays primary and 3x stays a higher-risk tier; keep the IEF off-leg (not bills, not TLT), the 15% gold, and the chop and vol-target rules. No correction changes a status on the Friday basis, and the only tranche flips are knife-edge.

2. Re-quote the in-sample reference numbers on the corrected panel (ALL1):
   - F2: Friday 19.4% / -24.0% / Calmar 0.81; tranche 16.9% / -27.7% / 0.61.
   - F3: Friday 23.4% / -29.8% / 0.79; tranche 20.2% / -31.8% / 0.63.

4. For future panel builds:
   - Add the dividend-neutral financing adjustment (QLD -1.05%/yr - 0.03*rf; TQQQ -1.91%/yr - 0.18*rf) and analytic par-bond duration before the ETF inception dates.

caveats: A_div keeps the sims price-only, so pre-inception NDX dividends (about 1%/yr in 2006-26; unknown from the panel before 1999) are still omitted. A_div is therefore a conservative financing correction. Crediting 2006-26-level dividends (A_lit) cuts the F3 cost from -0.62 to -0.08pp, and the truth is probably in between. QQQ before 1999 (the F1 sleeve and the QQQ benchmark) is also price-only and was not corrected.

Interbank spreads before 2006 were probably wider than in the 2010-26 calibration window. Only QLD 2006-09 samples a wide-spread regime. A_stress (2.15%/yr per unit borrowed) bounds this: F3 -0.99pp, F2 -0.44pp CAGR, with no extra flips on Fridays.

The financing regressions are noisy: intercept HAC SEs are 0.27-0.46%/yr, and the rf slopes in the dividend-neutral spec are not significant (QLD -0.03 +/- 0.09, TQQQ -0.18 +/- 0.13). The QLD dividend-neutral pooled fit fails its 2-SE stability test in 2010-15 (residual +0.37, se 0.18), where it is more punitive than the zero-rate actual.

The par-bond analytic model understates the ETFs' rate sensitivity in 2002-26 (k = 1.07 IEF, 1.12 TLT), and fits the 2022-26 sub-period worse than the fixed calibration (IEF TE 2.46 vs 2.32). The gate passed on the full window; B_k gives the same conclusions.

The pre-2000 gold source is a monthly-AVERAGE series. The step version (C1) still carries that smoothing, because no true month-end price series is in the panel. C2's +0.25pp CAGR comes from common.py's constant-mix convention (weights held constant every day) rebalancing a 36%-vol sleeve, not from miners' returns, which were lower (-5.87% vs -4.77%/yr, 1988-2000).

The pre-registered flip rule is sensitive to knife-edge items. The tranche flip of F2's QQQ-edge significance is within bootstrap Monte Carlo noise: the baseline's own status holds in only 4 of 5 seeds. I applied the rule as written; I judge the flip immaterial.

The duration and gold-shape diagnostics (fit-gate inputs) were inspected before the gate thresholds were written into the script. The thresholds had been chosen beforehand, and no strategy result was seen before the design was fixed. Smoke tests (20-100 bootstrap draws) re-ran the same 360 variants. The only design changes after them were the bootstrap column restriction (runtime) and the information-only seed check.
OOS is identical in every panel by construction: all corrections touch only data before 2010-02 (financing), before 2002-07 (bonds) and before 2000-08 (gold), and the OOS window uses real ETFs.

The fixed IEF/TLT calibration baked into panel.parquet was fit on data through 2026-11-17, about 4 months past the freeze, and was left as the baseline. The analytic refit uses data to 2026-07-24 only.

Variant count: 360 strategy variants (10 panels x 2 bases x 3 tiers x 6 configs, each tranche a 5-book average) plus the QQQ benchmark; 24 calibration fits; 20 decision bootstraps plus 24 information-only seed-check bootstraps.

verifications.rule_applied_correctly:
Yes, every pre-registered rule was applied exactly as written.

- **Flip rule** (status on corrected panel differs from P0, same code and basis): I recomputed it independently. Non-bootstrap items came from my own common.backtest engine. Bootstrap items came from my own cumprod bootstrap, which matches the specialist's seed-0 numbers to 5e-7. The flips reproduce exactly:
  - Friday basis: 0 of 48 items flip in all 9 corrected panels.
  - Tranche: ALL1 {R5|F2|calmar_ci_excl0}; ALL2 {R5|F2|calmar_ci_excl0, R6|F2|H1}; A_stress {R5|F2|calmar_ci_excl0}.
- **Duration gate**: B passes for IEF and TLT, so B goes into ALL1/ALL2 as the rule says. It also passes against a fixed calibration refit on data up to 2026-07-24 only (TLT: |gap| 0.310 vs threshold 0.380). The rule prefers B even though B_k also passed and fits better on all three gate metrics.
- **Bootstrap**: 63-day blocks, 2000 draws, seed 0, in-sample only, as pre-registered.
- **Reporting**: the specialist reported the 2 tranche items as formal conclusion changes and gave the 'immaterial' judgment separately, as the brief requires.
- **Only post-hoc element**: the information-only 5-seed check. It understates a systematic shift: over 20 seeds the tranche F2 edge is significant in 17/20 on P0 vs 9/20 under ALL1.

Verification scripts, all in update_2026_11/: r2_verify_model_hygiene_integrity_rerun.py, r2_verify_model_hygiene_integrity_checks.py, r2_verify_model_hygiene_integrity_boot.py (its extra-seeds section timed out under CPU contention and was removed after the run; sections 1-2 completed), r2_verify_model_hygiene_integrity_seeds.py (the 20-seed run; A_div did not finish, the other 4 panels did) and r2_verify_model_hygiene_integrity_alt.py. Outputs went only to the scratchpad; no other project file was modified.

verifications.lens: ROBUSTNESS. Checks: hidden selection (the specialist's 4 logged runs, exploration scripts); bootstrap design (block lengths 21/63/126/252, 20 seeds pooled to 40k draws, percentile-CI bias); alternative constructions that could flip the pre-registered statuses (the brief's literal financing fit, a dividend credit based on measured yields, a constant spread, level-matched B_k, TLT as a 25y par bond); period-boundary and single-episode dependence (1989-90, 2022); economic plausibility (NDX dividend yields measured from QQQ total return, gold-sleeve rebalancing mechanism).
verifications.rule_applied_correctly: Yes, applied exactly as written. Re-running r2_model_hygiene.py unchanged (output redirected to scratch) reproduces r2_model_hygiene.json with 0 differing numeric leaves. An independent rebuild through common.py (own par-bond code using numerical derivatives, own gold-step code) matches the default-config IS stats of A_div, B, C1, C2 and ALL1 to 5e-7. The rule is: status differs from P0 on the same basis, 63-day / 2000-draw / seed-0 percentile bootstrap, B used in the combinations because it passed the gate. It gives exactly what the specialist reports: Friday 0 flips under all 9 corrections; tranche R5|F2|calmar_ci_excl0 under ALL1 and ALL2 (primary) and A_stress (sensitivity), plus R6|F2|H1 under ALL2. The verdict is fragile, but the rule governs. (i) The tranche R5 flip appears at 63-day blocks only. With 21-day blocks P0 is already not significant. With 126-day blocks F3 flips instead of F2. With 252-day blocks nothing flips. (ii) There is no flip under the brief's literal financing regression (ALL1_lit). (iii) The ALL2 R6 flip vanishes if B_k replaces B. The TLT CAGR-gap gate criterion passed with only 0.07pp to spare (0.31 vs 0.38pp limit); a 0.15pp tolerance would have put B_k into the combinations.

verdicts.reason: My own regression code reproduces the pooled fits to <4e-7. Dividend-neutral: QLD alpha -1.054%/yr, beta -0.032; TQQQ -1.913%/yr, -0.176. Literal: +0.838/-0.175 and +1.266/-0.369. The regime means and QLD's 2010-15 stability failure (+0.37, se 0.18) also match. The dividend mechanism checks out: the NDX yield implied by QQQ total return minus NDX price averaged 0.98%/yr in 2010-26, consistent with the literal-minus-dividend-neutral intercept gaps of 1.89 and 3.18 (about lev x 1%). Alpha significance holds for HAC lags 5-250 and for monthly aggregation (SE: QLD 0.24-0.45, TQQQ 0.43-0.55). Minor wording issues: TQQQ's dividend-neutral beta SE is 0.125 (0.155 with monthly aggregation), not 0.13. The '0.7-1.4%/yr per unit borrowed' range omits QLD 2006-09 (2.15). 'Rising with the rate regime' is descriptive only: the pooled rf slopes are insignificant (QLD -0.03 +/- 0.09).
verdicts.corrected: TQQQ dividend-neutral beta -0.18 (se 0.12). Regime cost per unit borrowed 0.68-2.15%/yr (0.68-1.44 excluding QLD 2006-09).

verdicts.reason: My common.py rebuild of A_div gives: F3 Friday 23.52% / -30.3% / 0.775 (-0.62pp); F2 Friday 19.47% / -24.0% / 0.813 (-0.25pp); tranche -0.60 / -0.24pp; F3 H1 -1.11pp. Implied drags (-1.20 / -2.63%/yr) and pre-inception sleeve CAGRs (10.45% / -4.17%) also match. The claim's 'unless pre-inception dividends are credited' clause is decisive. Measured NDX yields were 0.42%/yr (2002-05) and 0.61% (2006-09). Crediting a smooth 0.5%/yr x lev on pre-inception days brings the net F3 financing cost to about -0.27pp, inside the critic's 0.2-0.5pp range (ALL1_div50 is -0.35pp including B and C1).

Gate inputs reproduce: IEF TE 2.21 vs 2.18%, corr 0.9477 vs 0.9474; TLT 5.05 vs 5.02, corr 0.9407 vs 0.9362. A closed-form par-bond price with numerical derivatives gives the same pre-2002 mean duration (5.83 / 10.75) and synthetic CAGR (9.28% / 10.20%). Strategy deltas of -0.09 to -0.13pp and F3 maxDD +0.6 / +0.9pp reproduce. Caveat: by yield bucket, pure B understates the real ETFs' rate sensitivity even at yields >= 4.5% (slope k 1.084 IEF, 1.078 TLT), while the fixed calibration overstates it there (k 0.956 / 0.868). So B_k is the better-supported pre-2002 extrapolation. Its deltas are smaller (-0.06 to -0.09pp), the same picture.

The numbers reproduce: C1 +0.02pp; C2 +0.235 / +0.248 / +0.252pp (F1/F2/F3 Friday). The mechanism attribution is mostly wrong. A weekly-drift backtest keeps +0.176 / +0.182 / +0.184pp; there, holdings drift between Friday marks and are reset at marks, and the engine reproduces common.backtest exactly when reset daily. So about 73% of the gain is not an artifact of common.py's every-day constant mix. It is the rebalancing premium of a fixed 15% weight in a 36%-vol sleeve: miners' arithmetic mean was +0.32%/yr against -4.86%/yr for interpolated gold (1988 to 2000-08). C1 also cannot test the monthly-average smoothing (interpolated vs GC=F monthly: corr 0.61, vol 12.9% vs 16.7%). 'Immaterial' therefore covers only booking-day timing.
verdicts.corrected: The C2 gain is about +0.18pp under weekly rebalancing; daily constant-mix adds only about 0.06-0.07pp of the +0.23-0.25pp.

verdicts.reason: My independent ALL1 rebuild matches every tier and basis to 5e-7. Friday: F1 11.80 / -19.2 / 0.615; F2 19.39 / -24.0 / 0.809; F3 23.44 / -29.8 / 0.787. Tranche: 10.80 / -20.8 / 0.520; 16.93 / -27.7 / 0.612; 20.17 / -31.8 / 0.634. The H1, since-2000 and ALL2 deltas match the JSON. The magnitude assumes zero pre-inception dividends: ALL1_lit gives F3 -0.16 / F2 -0.07pp (Friday), and a 0.5%/yr dividend credit gives -0.35 / -0.12pp.

Reproduced: Friday P(F2 > F3 excess Sharpe) 0.808 to 0.890; F3-F2 CAGR +4.42 [+1.83, +7.55] to +4.05 [+1.51, +7.13]. Robust to bootstrap design: across blocks of 21/63/126/252 days and all corrected panels, P(F2>F3) is at most 0.921 (A_stress tranche, 252-day blocks) and never reaches 0.95. The F3-F2 CAGR lower bound stays positive (minimum +0.31pp: A_stress tranche, 21-day blocks). F2's maxDD (-24.0% Friday) is shallower than F3's (-29.3% to -31.6%) in every panel tested.

Signs reproduce in all 10 panels and in my 5 alternative combinations (no R2 flip anywhere). Note that the tranche IS IEF edge for F2 / F3 (+0.115 / +0.049 under ALL1) comes entirely from H1. H2 is negative (-0.169 / -0.081) in every panel.

From the rerun, P(Calmar gold > IEF in the gold slot) is 0.448-0.611 across 10 panels x 3 tiers x 2 bases, far from the 0.05/0.95 thresholds. No R3 flip at block lengths 21/63/126/252 or in any alternative combination.

Numbers reproduce, and there is no R4 flip in any panel or alternative. The corrections cannot reach F2's H2: QLD is real from 2006-06-22, and the bond and gold corrections stop in 2002 and 2000. So F2's knife-edge H2 items (vol -0.006, chop -0.051) are immune. F3 tranche chop H2 moves only from +0.010 to +0.011.

The formal flip reproduces (seed 0: +0.0112 to -0.0016), and the Friday 'unchanged' holds at every block length. But 'within bootstrap noise / does not hold across seeds' is wrong at the limit. Pooled over 20 seeds (40k draws), the lower bound is +0.0094 at P0 (17/20 seeds > 0) and -0.0016 under ALL1 (9/20). That is a systematic -0.011 shift. The flip is, however, design-specific. With 21-day blocks P0 is not significant to begin with (-0.035), so nothing flips. With 126-day blocks F2 stays significant (+0.051 to +0.048) but F3 flips (+0.011 to -0.004) under ALL1, A_stress and ALL1_Bk. With 252-day blocks nothing flips (+0.082 to +0.072). The brief-literal ALL1_lit gives no flip (pooled +0.0071). The percentile CI is biased low: bootstrap mean 0.288 vs point estimate 0.446, because 63-day blocks break up QQQ's 2000-02 crash. The basic interval is [+0.27, +0.88] (P0) and [+0.26, +0.87] (ALL1).
verdicts.corrected: Under the 63-day percentile scheme, the tranche F2 Calmar-edge flip is systematic (pooled lower bound +0.009 to -0.002) but tiny (P 0.979 to 0.974). It depends on block length (none at 21 or 252 days; F3 instead at 126) and on the zero-dividend A_div spec.

verdicts.reason: The direction holds; the magnitude and framing are fragile. Under B itself the H1 reduction is 43-89%, not 62-89% (tranche F1 goes 0.183 to 0.105, -42.5%). Under B_k it is 33-72%. With TLT as a 25y par bond it is 29-82% (that model's yield-bucket slope is 0.92-1.00, the best scale fit). So 'about half', as the critic said. The 2002+ ETF data favour B_k or the 25y bond over pure B (B under-scales by about 8% even at yields >= 4.5%). The ALL2 R6|F2|H1 flip disappears under B_k (+0.011). 'Chiefly 2022' understates the dependence. Under ALL1 the 1988-2021 IEF-minus-TLT Calmar is -0.001 (F2 Friday), +0.010 (F3 Friday), +0.000 / +0.006 (tranche). 2007-21 favours TLT on Fridays (F2 -0.227, F3 -0.165). The whole IS edge comes from 2022-26 (+0.47 Friday; +0.34 / +0.40 tranche).
verdicts.corrected: The 1988-2006 IEF-over-TLT support shrinks by roughly half (29-89% across B, B_k and the 25y bond, tiers and bases). After correction, IEF over TLT is a single-episode (2022-26) result.

verdicts.reason: In the rerun, the OOS total difference vs P0 is 0.0 for all 9 corrected panels, 3 tiers and both bases, and H2 deltas for B and C are exactly 0.00. The corrections touch only days without a real series. OOS Friday -4.41 / -6.03 / -8.99%; tranche -6.61 / -10.69 / -14.91%.

issues: The headline haircut (F3 -0.70pp, F2 -0.33pp) assumes zero pre-inception dividends. A_div, the primary, departs from the brief's literal real-minus-sim regression. Under the literal spec in the combination (ALL1_lit = A_lit + B + C1) no status flips on either basis, and the haircut is F3 -0.16 / F2 -0.07pp (Friday) and -0.18 / -0.11pp (tranche). Measured NDX dividend yields (QQQ total return minus NDX price) were 0.42%/yr in 2002-05, 0.61% in 2006-09 and 0.98% in 2010-26. A smooth 0.5%/yr x lev credit on pre-inception days gives: F3 Friday 23.78% / -29.5% / 0.805 (-0.35pp); F2 19.59% / -24.0% / 0.818 (-0.12pp); tranche F3 20.51 / -31.6 / 0.648, F2 17.14 / -27.7 / 0.619. Recommendation 2 (re-quote ALL1 as the reference numbers) adopts the pessimistic end of a range whose pre-1999 input is unmeasured.

Bootstrap design drives the tranche R5 significance items. Flips by block length: 21 days none (P0 F2 already not significant, -0.035); 63 days F2; 126 days F3 under ALL1, A_stress and ALL1_Bk; 252 days none. The percentile CI of the F2/F3 Calmar edge vs QQQ is biased low: the bootstrap mean sits 0.16-0.30 below the point estimate because blocks break up QQQ's -83% 2000-02 drawdown. The pre-registered rule governs, but these items are close to arbitrary at the tranche margin.

The Friday 'no change' result is robust: 0 flips for ALL1, ALL2, A_stress, ALL1_lit, ALL1_Bk and ALL1_const at 21/63/126/252-day blocks. R1 P(excess Sharpe F2 > F3) never exceeds 0.921, and the F3-F2 CAGR lower bound never drops below +0.31pp.

Single-episode dependence, 1989-90: F3's IS maxDD sits in fully synthetic data (TQQQ sim, synthetic IEF, interpolated gold): 1989-10-09 to 1990-05-02 on both bases at P0, moving to 1995-07-17 to 1996-03-08 under B (Friday). Every F3 Calmar item is therefore a statistic of one synthetic episode, which every correction touches directly. F1 and F2 maxDDs are 2021-11 to 2022 real-ETF episodes that no correction can move, so F2's Calmar changes come only through CAGR.

Single-episode dependence, 2022: after correction the IEF-over-TLT case is entirely 2022-26. Under ALL1 the 1988-2021 Calmar difference is about 0 (F2 Friday -0.001, tranche +0.000), and 2007-21 favours TLT on Fridays (F2 -0.227, F3 -0.165).

The duration gate is loose and does not test yield scaling. By y(t-1) bucket, pure B's slope k is 1.05-1.09 for IEF and 1.08-1.15 for TLT at every yield level, while the fixed calibration falls to 0.956 / 0.868 at yields >= 4.5%. B_k (or TLT as a 25y bond) is the better-supported pre-2002 model. Per the rule B was used, and the ALL2 R6 H1 flip exists only because of that choice (ALL2_Bk F2 tranche H1 +0.011).

One alternative I tested (dividend-neutral model with QQQ total return on 1999-03 to inception days, ALL1_divQ) gave 2 Friday R6 H1 flips. I traced them to QQQ's AMEX 4:15pm close noise, not to dividends: QQQ-NDX daily TE was 11.25%/yr in 1999-03 to 2004-11 (lag-1 autocorrelation -0.50) vs 1.27% after 2009, and it creates a spurious 3-day -25.4% F2 maxDD (2000-01-03 to 01-06). Smooth credits (the measured 0.10%/yr for 1999-2005, and 0.50%/yr) give no flips (Friday F2/F3 H1 +0.015/+0.020 and +0.016/+0.023). I do not count it as a refutation, but post-correction R6 H1 margins (+0.005 to +0.020) are within path noise.

Hidden selection: none found. The specialist's 4 logged full runs (15:00-15:14) give identical statuses and flips. The only post-hoc addition is the disclosed information-only seed check. The exploration scripts (explore_fin, explore_dur, explore_gold) contain calibration diagnostics only, no strategy returns.

Multiple testing: 48 items x 9 corrections x 2 bases = 864 status comparisons. All 4 formal flips have margins under 0.02 Calmar (or a 0.013 move in a CI bound), which is consistent with knife-edge items crossing thresholds. No round-1 conclusion changes substantively.
Minor text errors. C1: TQQQ beta SE is stated as 0.13 (actual 0.125), and the per-unit cost range omits the 2.15%/yr regime. Key table: C2 Calmar range '-0.000' (minimum is +0.0003).

Reviewer variants and scripts: 396 strategy variants via the specialist's code (11 panels including 5 alternatives) plus 22 bootstraps; 48 block-length bootstraps; 80 two-column seed bootstraps; 4 dividend modes; 3 duration models; 1 weekly-drift engine. No outcome-tuned parameters: the 0.5% dividend credit is a round midpoint of measured yields, used as a sensitivity only. Scripts are in update_2026_11: r2_verify_model_hygiene_robustness_rerun.py, _checks.py (parts indep / alt / boot), _duration.py, _divq.py, _driftval.py. Outputs are in <scratchpad>/rob/ and <scratchpad>/rerun_mh_rob.json.

decisions.question: Is the Friday rebalance premium structural, and may it enter planning numbers?
decisions.decision: No. Plan only on the 5-weekday tranche. Treat Friday's in-sample premium as unplanned upside: +0.98 / +2.43 / +3.25pp CAGR and +0.09 to +0.20 Calmar for F1/F2/F3 at lag 1, and about half that with a one-session delay.
decisions.basis: Pre-registered rule: STRUCTURAL iff A and B. Both reviewers reproduced it exactly. A holds: F2 Friday minus tranche H1 +2.92pp / +0.192 Calmar, H2 +1.95pp / +0.175, placebo 99.3 / 99.6 pct. B fails: Friday beats the tranche on both CAGR and Calmar in 3 of 7 other markets (RUT on a +0.0001 Calmar margin, N225, IXIC); 5 were needed. Under the registered both-metric test, 0 of 48 alternative constructions reach 5/7. Supporting evidence: the 1988-99 first-holding-day mechanism has expired (Fri-to-Mon correlation 0.00 since 2007); the premium peaks at the tuned EMA-100 (A holds at only 2 of 7 EMA spans); Friday's H2 placebo rank is 93.9-96.2 pct under regular-spacing nulls; removing 2022 breaks A. Review rule (4) bars it from planning.

decisions.question: Which weekday should the live automation use?
decisions.decision: Keep the Friday close as the single fixed decision day, as in scanner.py and every reported number. Never move the signal to a Monday close. Expect a single book to scatter around the tranche, and judge the live record against a shadow 5-weekday tranche.
decisions.basis: friday_effect: no weekday is shown to be better, and a fixed day is operationally required. The 5 actual fixed-day F2 books have median 16.9% CAGR / -28.3% maxDD / Calmar 0.62 (maxDD range -24.0% to -33.2%), against the tranche's 17.3% / -27.7% / 0.62. Monday-close books were the worst in-sample (NDX F2 14.47% / -33.2%), though per half the Monday penalty holds in only 3 of 7 markets (weakened). The holiday-week convention is immaterial: gap +2.419pp vs +2.426pp.

decisions.question: Chop rule (half size when er20 < 0.25): retain, replace or remove?
decisions.decision: Pre-registered verdict: REPLACEABLE for F2 and F3. Keep it in the frozen spec unchanged, but classify it as an exposure dial and credit it with no edge. A simpler replacement, such as a constant ~0.71x exposure multiplier that halves turnover, needs its own pre-registered test first, because the multiplier is a new parameter.
decisions.basis: Tranche Calmar difference, B minus matched-exposure A, at 3 bps: F2 H1 +0.244 / H2 -0.012; F3 H1 +0.155 / H2 +0.007. H2 is below the +0.03 bar and the 7-market median is +0.0106 (at most +0.02), so REPLACEABLE. Both reviewers reproduced every input to 3e-11 or better, and the verdicts are unchanged at 10 and 15 bps. Removal is not supported, because no matched alternative beats B in-sample: A is lower by 0.055 / 0.119 Calmar, and the constant multiplier Ac is lower by 0.005 / 0.027 and behind B in all four tier-halves. Review rule (3) forbids a new tuned parameter. The matched-exposure edge was a 1990s era effect across markets; it reversed in 2000-06 and has been about zero since 2013.

decisions.question: Volatility target (scale = min(1, vt / vol20)): retain?
decisions.decision: Retain it in all tiers, unchanged. F2: REPLACEABLE (a de-levering dial). F3: INCONCLUSIVE, so retained by default as the rule specifies.
decisions.basis: F2: H1 +0.249 / H2 -0.002, cross-market median -0.0005, so REPLACEABLE. F3: H1 +0.159 / H2 +0.034, median -0.0005, so INCONCLUSIVE. This is a knife-edge: the H2 margin is +0.004, and the verdict flips to REPLACEABLE under lag 2, within-H2 re-matching, or H2 starts in 2003-05. The rule as written governs. The in-sample value comes from the 2000-02 bust: zeroing Mar-Dec 2000 turns the full-period difference to -0.013 / -0.042, and at matched exposure it is negative in 1988-99. Keeping it costs no turnover (12.87 vs 12.77 a year). The matched no-vol alternative has deeper drawdowns (F2 -34.0% vs -27.7%; F3 -47.4% vs -32.5%), and replacing it would need a new constant.

decisions.question: Re-tune any parameter now (EMA length, vol targets, chop threshold, gold weight, seasonality)?
decisions.decision: No. All July parameters stay frozen: EMA-100; vt 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.20; er20 threshold 0.25; chop multiplier 0.5; Aug-Sep x0.5; 15% gold; IEF off-leg.
decisions.basis: Review rule (3). Walk-forward re-picking had no out-of-sample skill: oracle minus pick was 0.175 / 0.185 Calmar. The model-input corrections flip 0 of 48 status items on the Friday basis and only 1-2 knife-edge items on the tranche. The 81-day out-of-sample window is information only.

decisions.question: Which tier: F1 (1x QQQ), F2 (2x QLD) or F3 (3x TQQQ)?
decisions.decision: Leverage is a risk dial, not an efficiency choice. F2 stays the reference tier for the paper build, as the user chose earlier. F1 is the lower-risk alternative and the most robust tier under stress. F3 is available on the US route only. Choose by the drawdown you can tolerate: the 1-in-20 drawdown is about -24% (F1), -37% to -40% (F2) and -46% to -51% (F3). This is a research classification, not personalised investment advice.
decisions.basis: IS88, US basis, L=252: F2 minus F3 Calmar -0.02 (P 0.33), excess Sharpe +0.015 (P 0.24); F2 minus F1 Calmar +0.10 (P 0.53), excess Sharpe -0.022 (P 0.67). CAGR gaps are significant: F3 is 3.6pp above F2, and F2 is 6.4pp above F1. Since 2000, excluding 2022, or on Ulcer-based measures, 1x is as efficient as or more efficient than 2x: F2-5050 minus F1-5050 excess Sharpe from 2000 is -0.105, 95% CI [-0.203, -0.005]. F1 was best in every adverse stress scenario and in both bear replays. No UCITS 3x fund exists.

decisions.question: Off-leg: IEF, 50/50 IEF + bills, bills, or TLT?
decisions.decision: Static IEF stays the default, and scanner.py must be corrected from TLT to IEF. The pre-specified 50/50 IEF/BIL split is optional insurance against a 2022-type stock-and-bond selloff, not an efficiency gain; if it is wanted, adopt it before the Nov 25 PCE release or not at all. Reject TLT and the duration-switching and bond-trend rules.
decisions.basis: 50/50 minus IEF, IS88: CAGR -0.95 to -1.06pp a year (P 0.99-1.00); excess Sharpe lower for F2 and F3 (P 0.98); Calmar gain not significant (P 0.19 / 0.60 / 0.72). That cost is mostly a falling-yield effect. Over IS88, IEF beat bills by 2.92pp a year while the 10y fell 4.15pp, and the 50/50 led by 1.0-1.3pp a year in 2020-26. At today's ~0.9pp term spread, its carry cost is about 0.2pp a year. A 100bp rise in the 10y today would cost the IEF book -5.7%, the 50/50 book -2.85% and an 85% TLT book -12.9%. After the duration correction, IEF over TLT rests on 2022-26 (the 1988-2021 Calmar difference is about 0), so it is a judgement. Round 1 found no off-leg rule that robustly beats static IEF.

decisions.question: Keep the 15% physical gold sleeve?
decisions.decision: Keep 15% physical gold (GLD; IGLN.L on the UCITS route) unchanged. Credit it only as de-levering and diversification, not as a drawdown edge.
decisions.basis: Gold vs IEF in the same 15% slot is a tie in all 10 model panels, all 3 tiers and both bases (P 0.45-0.61). Changing it after gold's bad out-of-sample quarter (GLD -7.8% since Oct 6) would be post-hoc selection. On trailing-year volatility, about half of today's off-leg risk is gold (Euler shares 48-52%).

decisions.question: What is the strategy's edge over QQQ buy-and-hold?
decisions.decision: Present it as drawdown avoidance, not extra return, and do not plan to beat QQQ's CAGR. In a bull market like 2010-26, expect F2 to trail QQQ by about 3pp a year with about 80% of its drawdown.
decisions.basis: IS88, US basis, L=252: Calmar edge F1 +0.33 (P 0.031), F2 +0.43 (P 0.019), F3 +0.45 (P 0.024). On the UCITS route P is 0.037-0.055, and none of the 3 tiers survives a Holm correction. The edge is significant only in windows that contain the 2000-02 crash: for starts after 2002-10, P is 0.12-0.33, and from 2007 it is 0.07-0.20. No CAGR edge is significant (F3 is borderline at P 0.052). Ulcer index is 4.5 / 9.7 / 13.7 against QQQ's 36.8. Since 2010 (reproduced in r2_final_checks.py): F2 15.82% / -27.8% / Ulcer 8.79 against QQQ 18.78% / -35.1% / 8.64; F3 21.83% / -31.5%. With the financing correction, F2's tranche Calmar edge becomes borderline: its CI excludes 0 in 17 of 20 bootstrap seeds at baseline but 9 of 20 after correction.

decisions.question: Do the model-input corrections (financing spread, yield-dependent duration, pre-2000 gold) change any conclusion?
decisions.decision: No conclusion changes. Apply the corrections as a planning haircut. Over 1988-2026 it is about -0.1pp CAGR for F1, -0.1 to -0.35pp for F2 and -0.2 to -0.7pp for F3. Since 2000 it is at most 0.35pp, and since 2007 about 0 for F2 and -0.14pp for F3. Describe F2's tranche Calmar edge over QQQ as 'borderline', and IEF over TLT as a 2022-26 result. Add the dividend-neutral financing fit and the level-matched (B_k) duration in future panel builds.
decisions.basis: The pre-registered flip rule was applied as written, and both reviewers confirmed it. On the Friday basis, 0 of 48 items flip under all 9 corrections. On the tranche, ALL1 flips 1 item (the F2 Calmar-edge CI lower bound moves from +0.011 to -0.002), and ALL2 flips 2 (adding F2 1988-2006 IEF minus TLT, +0.076 to -0.007). Both flips disappear under the literal financing fit, B_k duration or 252-day blocks. The -0.7pp F3 haircut assumes zero pre-inception dividends. The literal fit gives about -0.2pp, and a 0.5%/yr dividend credit gives -0.35pp.

decisions.question: Route: US-listed ETFs or UCITS?
decisions.decision: The backtest cannot settle this; legal and tax facts that the investor must confirm will. (1) Before funding anything, have a Pakistan-qualified cross-border adviser confirm four things: whether SBP FE Manual ch.20 para 13 covers this investment (one designated bank branch, USD 25k a year, repatriation of dividends and sale proceeds); the tax rate on foreign ETF gains (s.37A 15% vs slab rates up to 45%); tax residency; and the US estate-tax position. (2) If the investment is permitted and US-situs holdings stay below ~$60k, use the US route (QQQ/QLD/TQQQ + IEF + GLD), which is cheapest. (3) Above ~$60k, use the UCITS route: F2 via LQQ.PA + CBU0.L + IGLN.L, or F1 via CNDX.L + CBU0.L + IGLN.L. Plan it at least 1pp a year below the US route, and possibly 2-3pp; F3 is not available. Paper trading needs no funding and can start now. This is not tax or legal advice.
decisions.basis: The UCITS proxy (lag 2; 15 bps on the Nasdaq sleeve, 8 bps on the others) costs 0.94 / 1.13 / 1.23pp a year against the US route. Real-data UCITS gaps measured in round 1 were 1.0-3.2% a year, depending on the execution day: a structural ~1.1-1.4pp plus about +/-1-2pp a year of timing noise. LQQ.PA trades about $5.6m a day and is swap-based; CNDX.L is unlevered, and F1 gains +0.5pp a year if it trades at 8 bps. If the SBP cap applies, contributions alone would take 2-3 years to cross ~$60k, so the US route would serve first, and a later switch to UCITS would realise gains. If the repatriation requirement covers sale proceeds inside the account, weekly rebalancing may be infeasible under that regime. That is a go/no-go question for the whole strategy, not a route detail.

decisions.question: Execution timing and trade filter?
decisions.decision: US route: at 15:40-15:45 ET on the decision day, compute the signal from the live NDX and send market-on-close orders for the deltas. Fallback: compute the signal at the official close and execute at the next session's close. UCITS route: compute the signal at the official Friday US close and execute in Monday's European session while the US market is open (14:30-16:30 London), using limit orders. Apply a no-trade band of 2pp of NAV per sleeve, but always execute a risk-on/off switch in full.
decisions.basis: On the tranche, a one-session delay costs about 0 in every era (round 1), and the UCITS proxy already uses lag 2. The 2pp band cut orders from 132 to 56 a year with no return impact (round 1, verified). Letting weights drift weekly instead of the backtest's daily constant mix is immaterial: -0.05pp CAGR and -0.1pp maxDD for F2 (main_drift_check). The 15:45 pre-close signal is untested because there is no intraday data; its estimated cost falls on the Friday premium, which is not planned.

decisions.question: What numbers should planning use?
decisions.decision: Use the planning table: tranche basis, IEF off-leg, no Friday premium, with the model-input haircut. Treat each range's floor, which equals the since-2000 value in every row, as the base case and the rest as upside. US route: F1 9.1-10.6%, F2 13.1-17.0%, F3 16.7-21.6% CAGR. UCITS: about 1pp lower.
decisions.basis: The pre-registered planning rule was applied exactly: CAGR and Calmar = min..max over the 1988 / 2000 / 2007 starts on the US and UCITS bases, and maxDD from the L=252 stationary bootstrap. Both reviewers re-derived all 12 rows with 0 mismatches, and r2_final_checks.py reproduces the US rows; review rule (4) also applies. The floor is the prudent anchor because the table leaves out four drags: a parameter-selection haircut (the defaults sit at the 82nd-84th pct of the tranche grid), real UCITS frictions beyond the proxy, taxes, and any NDX drift below its 14.8%/yr history.

decisions.question: Review and stop triggers once live?
decisions.decision: Keep round 1's pre-commitments: review if the drawdown is worse than -35% (F2) or -45% (F3), or after 3 years behind QQQ with no bear market to explain it. Before running F1, pre-commit its equivalent level (its 1-in-20 drawdown, about -24% to -25%). A 12-month loss beyond the tranche's in-sample worst (-25.3% for F2) is a monitoring flag, not a trigger. Never re-tune in response to a flag.
decisions.basis: These are the round-1 critic's follow-ups. In the scenario stress, a plain repeat of 2022 from today's state breaches the specialist's proposed -21% flag in 2 of 21 start offsets, with maxDD as deep as -33%. The July finding that re-optimising chases noise still stands.

decisions.question: What must be fixed before the IBKR paper build?
decisions.decision: In scanner.py: (1) TLT -> IEF; (2) delete the yield-curve clause, which never changes a position; (3) output F2 as the reference tier, plus F1 and F3; (4) on holiday Fridays, use that week's last trading session; (5) append every decision and its inputs (C_t, EMA, vol20, er20, targets, orders, fills) to a CSV log; (6) compute a shadow 5-weekday tranche; (7) handle LQQ's 200:1 split (2026-07-09) in UCITS share maths; (8) add a dead-man's-switch alert. Then paper-trade for several months before funding.
decisions.basis: These are round 1's recommended follow-ups. Only 1 of the 17 out-of-sample decisions has a saved live record. The IBKR paper automation is the only open build item.

final.final_spec:
FINAL RULE SPEC: frozen July parameters, nothing re-tuned, decided weekly.

1. SIGNAL DATA. Use ^NDX (Nasdaq-100 price index) daily official closes C_t. Compute these at the decision close t:
- EMA100_t = EMA100_{t-1} + (2/101) x (C_t - EMA100_{t-1}). This is pandas ewm(span=100, adjust=False). Seed it on at least 500 sessions of history, which keeps the seed error below 0.01%.
- vol20_t = sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of the last 20 daily returns C_i/C_{i-1} - 1, times sqrt(252).
- er20_t = |C_t - C_{t-20}| / sum over i = t-19..t of |C_i - C_{i-1}|.

2. DECISION DAYS. Decide at every Friday NYSE close. If the Friday is an NYSE holiday, decide at that week's last trading session instead (e.g. Thu 2026-12-24, a 13:00 early close; Thu 2026-12-31). The backtest skipped such weeks; the two conventions differ immaterially (+2.419pp vs +2.426pp). Do not use a Monday-close signal.

3. RULE. Each tier has a Nasdaq sleeve and a vol target vt: F1 = QQQ, vt 0.20; F2 = QLD, vt 0.30 (reference tier); F3 = TQQQ, vt 0.20.
- risk_on = C_t > EMA100_t. This is identical to C_t > EMA100_{t-1}, so the bar is known after the prior close.
- scale = min(1, vt / vol20_t). If the decision date falls in August or September, scale = 0.5 x scale (the month of the decision date decides this).
- engine = 0 if not risk_on; = scale if er20_t >= 0.25; = 0.5 x scale if er20_t < 0.25.
- Targets: Nasdaq sleeve = 0.85 x engine; IEF = 0.85 - Nasdaq sleeve; physical gold = 0.15 at all times.
- No yield-curve clause, no macro overlays, no rate-shock or bond-trend switching.

4. INSTRUMENTS
- US route (US-situs holdings below ~$60k): QQQ / QLD / TQQQ, IEF, GLD (as backtested).
- UCITS route: F2 uses LQQ.PA (Amundi Nasdaq-100 2x; EUR quote of the USD index; adjust share maths for the 200:1 split of 2026-07-09); F1 uses CNDX.L; IEF -> CBU0.L; GLD -> IGLN.L. F3 has no UCITS route.
- Pre-specified option, not the default, to be decided before 2026-11-25 or never: a 50/50 IEF/BIL off-leg, with IEF = BIL = 0.5 x (0.85 - Nasdaq sleeve).

5. EXECUTION
- US: at 15:40-15:45 ET (12:40-12:45 on 13:00 early-close days), compute the signal with the live NDX as C_t. Send market-on-close orders for the deltas before the 15:50 ET MOC cut-off. Fallback: compute the signal at the official close and execute at the next session's close (no planning impact).
- UCITS: compute the signal at the official Friday US close. Execute in Monday's European session while the US market is open (14:30-16:30 London), using limit orders. If Monday is a European holiday, use the next overlapping session.

6. TRADE FILTER. For each sleeve, skip the trade if |target - held| <= 2pp of NAV. A risk-on/off switch always moves every sleeve to target. Between decisions, positions drift freely; this is immaterial against the backtest (F2 -0.05pp a year).

7. COST BUDGET. At most 5 bps per unit traded on the US route (the planning basis). About 15 bps on the Nasdaq sleeve and 8 bps on IEF and gold on the UCITS route.

8. LOGGING AND REVIEW
- Write one CSV row per decision: C_t, EMA100_{t-1}, vol20, er20, risk_on, chop flag, targets, orders and fills.
- Track a shadow 5-weekday tranche to judge results against the plan.
- Review if the drawdown is worse than -35% (F2) or -45% (F3), or after 3 years behind QQQ with no bear market to explain it. For F1, pre-commit about -25% before going live.
- No re-tuning.

9. EXPECTATIONS. Use the planning table (tranche basis, no Friday premium). Base case = range floor: US F1 9.1%, F2 13.1%, F3 16.7% CAGR, with 1-in-20 drawdowns of about -24% / -37% to -40% / -46% to -51%. The edge is drawdown avoidance, not beating QQQ's return.

TODAY'S EXPOSURE IS THE OFF-LEG ONLY. All 15 books (3 tiers x 5 weekdays) hold 85% IEF + 15% GLD and no equity.
- Instant shocks: 10y +100bp = -5.7% (a pure 1-month shock simulates at -5.68pp); 10y -100bp = +6.35%; gold -15% = -2.25%; the first and third together = -7.95%.

- A +100bp move within one month is a 5.4-sigma move with no 1988-2026 precedent (largest: +95bp). A 15% gold fall within two months is 1.4-sigma.

RE-ENTRY MECHANICS.
- Near-term re-entries will be halved by the chop rule. er20 will be about 0-0.07, because the closes 20 sessions back (10-23 and 10-29) sit at or above the bar.
- Halved, F2/F3 hold about 0.6-0.7x NDX and F1 about 0.2x. The full 1.44x size needs er20 >= 0.25.
- In the specialist's 30%-vol paths, 40-55% of first re-entries were halved.

V-REBOUND (S3: back to the 31,224 record in 6 weeks, then +1%/month).
- The Friday re-entry median falls on 2026-12-04 to 12-11, at NDX about 29,540-29,650 (+9-10%), after 62-64% of the climb.
- Only about 44-50% of the rebound is earned.
- 12-month F2 return: -3% to +2% depending on the noise construction (tranche -3% to +7%), against QQQ +22.5% and QLD +31%.
- The roughly 25pp shortfall breaks down as 7.8pp entry lag, 13.3pp post-entry exits and whipsaws, and 3.5pp sizing drag (500 seeds).
- If volatility calms after the rebound (S3c), F2 makes +3% to +4%.

BEAR MARKETS.
- 2022-like (S4: NDX -25% over 6 months, 10y +75bp, gold -10%): F2 12-month -9.4% to -9.9% (median maxDD -17.6%), F1 -3.7%, F3 about -10% to -11%, against QQQ -25.2% and QLD -51.2%.

- Re-entering on bear-market rallies costs 3.5-13pp against never re-entering, depending on how the noise is constructed.

HISTORICAL PATHS REPLAYED FROM TODAY'S STATE (single paths; the robustness reviewer tested start offsets of +/-10 days).
- F2 beats QQQ robustly only on the 2000 path (21/21 offsets; F2 -9.6% vs QQQ -53.7% and QLD -86.2%), the 2022 path (18/21) and the 1990 path.

- In strong-trend rebounds, F2 captured roughly 60-85% of QQQ's return.

TRENDLESS MARKETS ARE THE MAIN UNPROTECTED REGIME.
- A flat year at 30% vol gives F2 a median of -2.4% to -7.4%, depending on construction. In-sample flat, high-vol analogs were V-shaped and gave +18.7%, so this loss comes from the model's assumptions.

- Those whipsaw rates (5-6 per 6 months) exceed anything in-sample (maximum 4).

TIERS UNDER STRESS.

- F2 and F3 behave almost identically while vol20 is above 30%: their NDX beta is the same (0.51 / vol20).

MONITORING.

- Pinning every path at day 252 lowers F2 medians by 3-5pp against free noise.
